# MylesNet

[[MylesNet]] is the [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] WiFi hotspot and connectivity management SaaS for East African internet resellers, estate networks, market operators, hospitality businesses, small ISP partners, and public-access WiFi operators.

## Product Snapshot

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Company | [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] |
| Owner | [[Jonathan Myles]] |
| Stage | Production foundation implementation |
| Primary users | Internet resellers, hotspot operators, estate network managers, hospitality operators, market WiFi operators, and support teams |
| Strategic role | Connectivity SaaS product line and local infrastructure operations platform |

## Product Purpose

[[MylesNet]] helps local connectivity operators manage tenants, hotspot packages, vouchers, subscriber access, payments, network operations, and support workflows from one operational system. It should be practical for East African connectivity realities, including mobile money, field agents, local support, unreliable infrastructure, and small teams running revenue-critical networks.

## Current State

[[MylesNet]] has an active vault product folder, a detailed [[products/mylesnet/MylesNet_Master_Technical_Specification_v3|MylesNet Technical Specification]], [[WorkOS AuthKit]] app-boundary notes, [[Convex]] deployment history, and active blockers around [[Linear]], production [[Vercel]] mapping, provider configuration, and final launch verification.

## Core Capabilities

- Platform administration for [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] staff.
- Network operator administration for resellers and network owners.
- Tenant dashboard for hotspot and subscriber operations.
- Hotspot package and voucher management.
- Subscriber and device session visibility.
- Payment and wallet workflows using [[M-Pesa Daraja]] and related mobile money providers where approved.
- Field agent support workflows.
- Audit logs and role-based access control.
- Operational reports for revenue, usage, customers, and network health.

## Key Risks

- Authentication and RBAC must stay correct across platform, network, and tenant scopes.
- Cookie security must be verified over production domains before launch.
- Provider credentials, callback URLs, webhook secrets, and production environment variables must be confirmed before deployment.
- Payment and connectivity operations require clear audit trails and support workflows.

## Product Folder

- [[products/mylesnet/overview|MylesNet Overview]]
- [[products/mylesnet/about|MylesNet About]]

## Implementation Standards

[[MylesNet]] must follow [[Agent Operating Standard]], [[Development Phase Order]], [[Panel Naming Convention]], [[Code Standards]], [[Testing Standards]], [[No Placeholder UI]], [[Git And Deployment Standards]], [[WorkOS AuthKit]], [[Cookie Handling]], [[CSRF Protection]], and [[Secrets And Environment Variables]].

## Footer And Social Links

The [[MylesNet]] landing page must follow [[Footer Standards]], [[Landing Page Standards]], and [[Social Links]]. Required footer copy: © 2026 Powered by [MylesCorp Technologies Ltd](https://mylescorptech.com/) · All rights reserved. Social links must use the canonical [[LinkedIn]], [[Facebook]], [[Twitter]], [[YouTube]], [[Instagram]], and [[TikTok]] URLs.

## Current Blockers

- [[Linear]] connector remains unavailable in current [[Codex]] sessions.
- Production [[Vercel]] project mapping must be confirmed.
- Live [[WorkOS AuthKit]] values, callback URIs, and webhook secret must be configured.
- Payment and SMS provider credentials must be confirmed before production deployment.
- Production cookie headers must be verified after deployment.

# WorkOS AuthKit

[[WorkOS AuthKit]] is the approved authentication and authorization layer for every [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] product and client project.

Secret names and storage locations are tracked in [[Secrets And Environment Variables]]. Live values must never be written into this note.

## Required Usage

- Use [[WorkOS AuthKit]] for login, callback handling, sessions, and organization membership.
- Use server-side session helpers in [[Next.js]].
- Verify roles on the server before rendering protected pages or running mutations.
- Redirect unauthenticated users to `/login`.
- Redirect insufficient roles to `/unauthorized`.

## RBAC Panels

| Panel | URL | WorkOS Org | Roles |
|---|---|---|---|
| Master Admin | `admin.[product].com` | `[Product] Platform Org` | `platform-owner`, `platform-admin`, `platform-support` |
| Super Admin | `network.[product].com` | `[Product] Network Org` | `network-owner`, `network-admin`, `network-agent`, `operator_manager` |
| Agency Panel | `agency.[product].com` | `[Product] Agency Org` | `agency_super_admin` |
| Reseller Panel | `reseller.[product].com` | `[Product] Reseller Org` | `reseller_super_admin` |
| Partner Panel | `partner.[product].com` | `[Product] Partner Org` | `partner_admin`, `partner_user` |
| Affiliate Panel | `affiliate.[product].com` | `[Product] Affiliate Org` | `affiliate_admin`, `affiliate_user` |
| Tenant App | `[tenant].[product].com` | `[Product] Tenant Org` | `tenant-admin`, product-specific tenant roles |

## WorkOS Organization Model

Every product needs separate [[WorkOS]] organizations for:

- Production (environment-level)
- Staging (environment-level)
- Platform admin panel scope
- Network admin panel scope
- Agency panel scope (if applicable)
- Reseller panel scope (if applicable)
- Partner panel scope (if applicable)
- Affiliate panel scope (if applicable)
- Tenant app scope (per-tenant)

Every tenant must have its own dedicated organization. Never share one [[WorkOS]] organization across two products or tenants.

### Independent Organizations for External Roles

Partner, Affiliate, and Reseller roles must have their own independent [[WorkOS]] organizations, separate from the Tenant organization:

- **Partner Org**: `[Product] Partner Org` - Dedicated organization for partner integrations and API access
- **Affiliate Org**: `[Product] Affiliate Org` - Dedicated organization for affiliate marketing and referral programs
- **Reseller Org**: `[Product] Reseller Org` - Dedicated organization for reseller operations and territory management

These independent organizations ensure proper isolation and RBAC boundaries for external business relationships.

## Convex Requirements

Every [[Convex]] function touching user data must:

- Call `getAuthUserId(ctx)` first.
- Reject if the caller is unauthenticated.
- Load the user's role from the users table.
- Check permissions before reading or writing data.
- Scope every query by `tenantId`.

Every project must include `convex/lib/auth.ts` helpers:

- `requireAuth(ctx)`
- `requireRole(ctx, roles[])`
- `requireTenant(ctx, tenantId)`
- `requireNetwork(ctx, networkId)`
- `requireAgency(ctx, agencyId)`
- `requireReseller(ctx, resellerId)`
- `requirePartner(ctx, partnerId)`
- `getPlatformContext(ctx)`

## Webhooks

Every project must configure these [[WorkOS]] webhooks:

- `user.created`
- `user.updated`
- `user.deleted`
- `organization_membership.created`
- `organization_membership.updated`
- `organization_membership.deleted`
- `session.created`
- `session.revoked`

Webhook endpoint pattern: `https://[product].com/api/webhooks/workos`.

## WorkOS MCP For Configuration Management

For all [[WorkOS]] configuration, organization management, SSO setup, role configuration, webhook configuration, and dashboard operations, agents must use [[WorkOS MCP]] instead of manual dashboard navigation or direct API calls.

### When To Use WorkOS MCP

Use [[WorkOS MCP]] for:

- Creating and configuring [[WorkOS]] organizations (Production, Staging, Platform, Network, Tenant)
- Setting up SSO connections and troubleshooting IdP issues
- Configuring webhooks and monitoring delivery
- Managing roles and permissions
- Configuring branding (logos, colors, CSS)
- Setting up feature flags
- Managing API keys
- Reviewing audit logs
- Environment configuration
- Any other [[WorkOS]] dashboard operations

### MCP Integration Pattern

1. Start with `whoami` to verify permissions
2. Use `list_operations` to discover available operations
3. Use `query` for read operations (viewing organizations, webhooks, etc.)
4. Use `mutate` for write operations (creating organizations, configuring webhooks, etc.)
5. For destructive operations, call `mutate` twice with `confirm: true`

### Example: Creating Organization Configuration

Instead of manually navigating the [[WorkOS]] dashboard:

```bash
# Agent uses MCP to create organization
mcp1_mutate operation="createOrganization" variables={
  "environmentId": "environment_xxx",
  "name": "EduMyles Production",
  "allowProfilesOutsideOrganization": false
}
```

### Security Benefits

- Inherits your exact dashboard permissions
- No separate permission model to maintain
- Destructive operations require confirmation
- Secrets are stripped from responses
- Full product surface access

## Session Token Lifecycle

WorkOS AuthKit manages session tokens internally. You do not handle JWTs manually.

- **Session cookie (`__[product]_session`):** This is the access token equivalent. 24-hour lifetime, refreshed on activity. `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite: lax`, scoped to the correct panel domain.
- **Tenant context cookie (`__[product]_tenant`):** Same security attributes as session cookie. Cleared when session clears or when tenant switches.
- **Refresh token:** Managed transparently by the AuthKit SDK. Your code does not touch it.
- **Role change:** When WorkOS sends `organization_membership.created` or `.deleted`, clear the session cookie immediately and force re-authentication. Never cache role data beyond one request.

## Webhook Sync Sequence

When a WorkOS webhook arrives, process in this exact order:

1. Validate the WorkOS signature using `WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
2. Parse the event type and payload.
3. If `user.created`: insert into Convex `users` table with `workosUserId`, `email`, `role` (default to lowest permitted role), `tenantId` (if applicable), `createdAt`.
4. If `user.updated`: upsert the user record, sync email and name changes.
5. If `user.deleted`: soft delete in Convex (`deletedAt = Date.now()`), clear all active sessions, log the event.
6. If `organization_membership.created`: assign the role to the user in Convex `users` table, update `organizationId`, log the assignment.
7. If `organization_membership.deleted`: revoke the role, clear the session cookie, force re-authentication, log the revocation.
8. Always return HTTP 200 to WorkOS immediately after validation, before any Convex mutation.
9. If Convex mutation fails, log the error server-side and retry via a scheduled function. Never return 4xx/5xx to WorkOS.

- Official docs: [WorkOS AuthKit Docs](https://workos.com/docs/authkit)
- Next.js sessions: [Configure a Next.js Session](https://workos.com/docs/user-management/1-configure-your-project/configure-a-session/nextjs)
- Organizations: [Organizations](https://workos.com/docs/organizations)
- Roles and permissions: [Roles](https://workos.com/docs/user-management/roles)
- Webhooks: [WorkOS Webhooks](https://workos.com/docs/events)
- Changelog: [WorkOS Changelog](https://workos.com/changelog)

Agents must check these provider docs before implementing [[WorkOS AuthKit]] login, callback, session, organization, role, webhook, or cookie behavior. When [[WorkOS]] publishes a new release, security requirement, or AuthKit migration guide, update this note, [[Tech Stack]], and [[context/tech-stack|Tech Stack Context]] before coding against the new behavior.

## Role Definitions

### Master Admin Roles
- `platform-owner`: Full platform control, can manage all organizations, networks, agencies, resellers, partners
- `platform-admin`: Platform administration, can manage organizations, networks, agencies, resellers, partners
- `platform-support`: Read-only platform access for support operations

### Super Admin Roles
- `network-owner`: Full control over own network organizations
- `network-admin`: Network administration, can manage network organizations
- `network-agent`: Limited network operations access
- `operator_manager`: Manages own network + assigned agencies/resellers/partners

### Agency Panel Roles
- `agency_super_admin`: Full control over agency client base, billing, commissions, white-label settings

### Reseller Panel Roles
- `reseller_super_admin`: Full control over reseller client base, territories, revenue, commissions, sub-resellers

### Partner Panel Roles
- `partner_admin`: Full control over partner integrations, API keys, webhooks
- `partner_user`: Read-only access to partner integration data

### Tenant App Roles (Product-Specific)

**EduMyles:** `tenant-admin`, `teacher`, `finance-officer`, `parent`, `student`, `principal`, `head_of_department`, `staff_hr`, `librarian`

**MylesNet:** `client_admin`, `manager`, `technician`, `user`

**AgriMyles:** `client_admin`, `farm_manager`, `operator`, `technician`, `viewer`

## Never Do

- Never store passwords in product code.
- Never expose `WORKOS_API_KEY` to client code.
- Never allow self-assigned roles.
- Never share organizations across tenants.
- Never cache role data beyond one request.
- Never allow agency A to access agency B client data.
- Never allow reseller A to access reseller B client data.
- Never allow partner to access organization data directly.

[[WorkOS]] is the identity platform behind the approved [[WorkOS AuthKit]] authentication and authorization standard for [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] products.

## Provider Documentation

- Official docs: [WorkOS Docs](https://workos.com/docs)
- User Management: [User Management](https://workos.com/docs/user-management)
- AuthKit: [AuthKit](https://workos.com/docs/authkit)
- Organizations: [Organizations](https://workos.com/docs/organizations)
- Events and webhooks: [Events](https://workos.com/docs/events)
- Changelog: [WorkOS Changelog](https://workos.com/changelog)
- MCP Server: [WorkOS Management MCP Server](https://workos.com/blog/management-mcp-server)
- MCP Docs: [WorkOS MCP Documentation](https://workos.com/docs/mcp)

Agents must check these provider docs before implementing [[WorkOS]] identity, organization, role, webhook, or session behavior. When [[WorkOS]] publishes a new release, security requirement, or migration guide, update this note, [[WorkOS AuthKit]], [[Tech Stack]], and [[context/tech-stack|Tech Stack Context]] before coding against the new behavior.

[[WorkOS]] is the identity platform used by [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] for authentication, organization management, and role-based access control across internal products and client projects.

## Role In The Tech Stack

- Primary auth platform through [[WorkOS AuthKit]].
- Organization model for product environments, panels, and tenants.
- RBAC source for platform, network, and tenant roles.
- Webhook source for syncing users and organization membership changes into [[Convex]].

## MylesCorp Rule

[[WorkOS]] is mandatory for all auth work. Do not use [[NextAuth]], [[Clerk]], [[Auth0]], [[Supabase Auth]], [[Firebase Auth]], or another identity provider in [[EduMyles]], [[MylesCRM]], [[AgriMyles]], [[MylesCare]], [[MylesProp]], [[EduRyde]], [[MylesNet]], [[PhysioHome]], or future [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] products.

Credentials must live only in `.env.local`, deployment environment variables, or [[Jonathan Myles]]'s password manager. Never write live [[WorkOS]] keys, webhook secrets, cookie passwords, client secrets, or organization IDs into vault notes, source code, comments, [[Linear]], or logs.

Use [[Secrets And Environment Variables]] as the canonical registry for variable names and approved storage locations. Do not copy values from chat into the vault.

## Organization Model

Every product needs separate [[WorkOS]] organizations for:

- Production.
- Staging.
- Platform admin panel.
- Network admin panel.
- Tenant app scope.

Every tenant must have its own dedicated organization. Never share one [[WorkOS]] organization across two products or tenants.

## Required Project Variables

- `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`
- `WORKOS_API_KEY`
- `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD`
- `WORKOS_ORG_ID`
- `WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`

## WorkOS Management MCP Server

[[WorkOS MCP]] is the mandatory method for all AI agent interactions with [[WorkOS]] in [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] workflows. The MCP server gives agents the same access to [[WorkOS]] as your dashboard login, inheriting your exact roles and permissions.

### Why MCP Is Mandatory

- **Security**: Inherits your exact dashboard permissions, no separate permission model
- **Consistency**: All agents use the same interface
- **Safety**: Destructive operations require confirmation, secrets are stripped
- **Completeness**: Full product surface access
- **Discoverability**: list_operations pattern for finding operations

### MCP Tools

- **whoami**: Returns authenticated user identity and capabilities
- **list_operations**: Discovers available operations
- **query**: Read operations for data retrieval
- **mutate**: Write operations for data changes (requires confirm for destructive actions)

### Connection Details

- **Server URL**: `https://mcp.workos.com/mcp`
- **Authentication**: OAuth consent required
- **Scope**: Full product surface except credential-minting, impersonation, billing, account administration

See [[WorkOS MCP]] for detailed usage patterns and examples.

# Multi-Tenancy Enforcement Standards

[[Multi-Tenancy Enforcement Standards]] define tenant isolation rules for every product using [[Convex]], [[Next.js]], and [[WorkOS AuthKit]].

## Golden Rule

Every [[Convex]] function that reads or writes tenant data must scope by `tenantId`. Returning tenant data without tenant scoping is a critical security bug.

**Extended Golden Rule:**
- Agency functions must scope by `agencyId`. Agency A cannot access Agency B client data.
- Reseller functions must scope by `resellerId`. Reseller A cannot access Reseller B client data.
- Partner functions must scope by `partnerId`. Partners cannot access organization, network, agency, or reseller data directly.
- Network functions must scope by `networkId`. Network A cannot access Network B data.
- Platform functions can access all data but must enforce role-based access control.

## Subdomain Resolution

Middleware must resolve context from subdomain on every request:

### Tenant App Subdomain Resolution
1. Extract subdomain from the request host header.
2. Look up tenant in [[Convex]] by subdomain slug.
3. If not found, show a professional 404 page.
4. If status is not `active`, show the correct status page.
5. Attach `tenantId` to request headers for server components.

### Agency Panel Subdomain Resolution
1. Extract `agency.[product].com` subdomain.
2. Look up agency in [[Convex]] by subdomain slug.
3. If not found, show 404 page.
4. Attach `agencyId` to request headers.

### Reseller Panel Subdomain Resolution
1. Extract `reseller.[product].com` subdomain.
2. Look up reseller in [[Convex]] by subdomain slug.
3. If not found, show 404 page.
4. Attach `resellerId` to request headers.

### Partner Panel Subdomain Resolution
1. Extract `partner.[product].com` subdomain.
2. Look up partner in [[Convex]] by subdomain slug.
3. If not found, show 404 page.
4. Attach `partnerId` to request headers.

### Master Admin Subdomain Resolution
1. Extract `admin.[product].com` subdomain.
2. Verify platform admin role.
3. Attach platform context to request headers.

### Super Admin Subdomain Resolution
1. Extract `network.[product].com` subdomain.
2. Look up network in [[Convex]] by subdomain slug.
3. Attach `networkId` to request headers.

Never trust `tenantId`, `agencyId`, `resellerId`, `partnerId`, or `networkId` from the client.

## Tenant Status

- `active` means full access.
- `suspended` means read-only access with suspension banner.
- `deactivated` means no access and reactivation page.
- `plan_expired` means limited access and billing redirect.
- `pending_setup` means redirect to onboarding.

Check tenant status on every request in middleware.

## Query Pattern

```ts
const records = await ctx.db
  .query("table_name")
  .withIndex("by_tenant", q => q.eq("tenantId", args.tenantId))
  .filter(q => q.eq(q.field("deletedAt"), undefined))
  .paginate(args.paginationOpts)
```

Never collect and then filter by tenant.

## Isolation Testing

Before every deployment touching tenant-scoped functions:

### Tenant Isolation Testing
1. Create two test tenants.
2. Create records in tenant A.
3. Sign in as tenant B.
4. Confirm tenant B cannot access tenant A data.
5. Document the result in the pull request.

### Agency Isolation Testing
1. Create two test agencies.
2. Provision clients under Agency A.
3. Sign in as Agency B admin.
4. Confirm Agency B cannot access Agency A client data.
5. Document the result in the pull request.

### Reseller Isolation Testing
1. Create two test resellers.
2. Provision clients under Reseller A.
3. Sign in as Reseller B admin.
4. Confirm Reseller B cannot access Reseller A client data.
5. Document the result in the pull request.

### Partner Isolation Testing
1. Create test partner.
2. Create test organization with integration data.
3. Sign in as partner user.
4. Confirm partner cannot access organization data directly.
5. Confirm partner can only access integration data.
6. Document the result in the pull request.

### Network Isolation Testing
1. Create two test networks.
2. Create organizations under Network A.
3. Sign in as Network B operator.
4. Confirm Network B cannot access Network A organization data.
5. Document the result in the pull request.

## Cross-Panel Data Flow Rules

### operator_manager Cross-Panel Access
- operator_manager can view and manage: own network organizations + assigned agencies + assigned resellers + assigned partners
- operator_manager cannot: access other networks, platform settings, or unassigned agencies/resellers/partners
- All queries must include networkId filter and optional agencyId/resellerId/partnerId filters

### Agency Client Base Isolation
- Agency A can only view and manage clients they provisioned
- Agency A cannot view Agency B clients under any circumstance
- Commission tracking is scoped to agencyId

### Reseller Client Base Isolation
- Reseller A can only view and manage clients they sold
- Reseller A cannot view Reseller B clients under any circumstance
- Territory management is scoped to resellerId
- Sub-reseller hierarchy is scoped to parent resellerId

### Partner Integration Data Isolation
- Partners can only access their own integration data
- Partners cannot access organization, network, agency, or reseller data directly
- API keys and webhooks are scoped to partnerId

## Related Standards

- [[Convex Schema And Function Standards]]
- [[WorkOS AuthKit]]
- [[Cookie Handling]]
- [[Testing Standards]]
- [[Panel Naming Convention]]
- [[intelligence/rbac-permissions-reference|RBAC Permissions Reference]] - For field-level security rules and column-level access control
- [[Role-Based UI Visibility Standards]]

216: ## 1. Executive Summary
217: 
218: [[MylesNet]] is a multi-tenant ISP and WiFi hotspot management SaaS platform built by [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] for East African connectivity operators. It serves hotspot operators, WiFi service providers, estate network managers, hospitality venues, campus networks, community networks, and eventually larger ISP operations with a complete suite of customer management, package and voucher sales, payment processing, financial analytics, network device inventory, support ticketing, communications, and customer self-service capabilities.
219: 
220: ### Business Context
221: 
222: [[Jonathan Myles]] operates a real WiFi reselling business in Uganda and Kenya. [[MylesNet]] is being built as both the operational tool for that business (dogfood/first-tenant case) and as a SaaS product for other operators. The product must work in the field -- on low-end Android phones in direct sunlight, on unreliable network connections, with mobile money as the primary payment method.
223: 
224: ### Business Model
225: 
226: Subscription-based SaaS with three tiers:
227: 
228: | Plan | Target Operator | UGX Price | KES Price | Capability |
229: |---|---|---|---|---|
230: | Starter | Single-site operator | UGX 28,000/mo | KSh 1,000/mo | One location, limited customer count, core registration, payment recording, basic analytics |
231: | Growth | Growing operator | UGX 78,000/mo | KSh 2,800/mo | Multiple locations, full analytics, CSV exports, SMS reminders, staff roles |
232: | Pro | Multi-site or franchise | UGX 196,000/mo | KSh 7,000/mo | Unlimited locations, white-label controls, API access, advanced integrations, priority support |
233: 
234: UGX is the primary currency (no decimal places). KES is secondary. Exact prices require [[Jonathan Myles]] confirmation before public display.
235: 
236: Additionally, the platform supports:
237: - 21-day free trial for new operators (per screenshot 00, starting at USh 25,000/month after trial)
238: - Referral program: 20% commission on referred operator subscription payments for 12 months (per screenshot 14)
239: - Voucher agent commissions and withdrawal flows
240: 
241: ### Seven-Tier Hierarchy Fit
242: 
243: [[MylesNet]] fits the [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] seven-tier panel hierarchy:
244: 
245: | Tier | MylesNet Implementation |
246: |---|---|
247: | 1. Platform Admin | `/platform` in `apps/admin` -- [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] internal control |
248: | 2. Network Operator | `/admin` in `apps/network` -- ISP/hotspot operator workspace |
249: | 3. Operator Manager | `/admin` with elevated permissions -- regional operator oversight |
250: | 4. Agency Super Admin | `/admin` with agency scope -- agency client management |
251: | 5. Reseller Super Admin | `/admin` with reseller scope -- reseller client management |
252: | 6. Partner Admin | Future partner API integration tier |
253: | 7. Client Admin / End User | `/dashboard` in `apps/web` -- customer self-service |

462: ## 4. Network Layer Architecture
463: 
464: ### MikroTik Router Integration
465: 
466: [[MylesNet]] operators primarily use [[MikroTik]] RouterOS hardware for hotspot and PPPoE access control. The platform supports two access modes visible in screenshots 03, 04, 32, and 38:
467: 
468: #### Hotspot Mode (Primary)
469: - Captive portal authentication via voucher code or MAC-Cookie auto-reconnect
470: - Device remember duration configurable per tenant (default 30 days per screenshot 32)
471: - Auto-reconnect methods: MAC-Cookie (recommended), HTTP Cookie, or IP Binding
472: - Captive portal theming: template selection, background image upload, brand color override, gradient end color, font selection, and language (per screenshot 32)
473: - Redirect URL after successful login configurable per tenant
474: - Prune inactive users setting (default 30 days per screenshot 32)
475: 
476: #### PPPoE Mode
477: - PPPoE username/password authentication (screenshot 04)
478: - PPPoE subscription portal URL configurable per tenant (screenshot 30)
479: - Status tracking: Online, Offline, Active, Pending Registrations, Expired (per screenshot 04)
480: 
481: ### IP Binding Management
482: 
483: Per screenshot 03, IP bindings allow specific devices to bypass hotspot authentication:
484: - Bind IP action creates a static binding on the linked MikroTik router
485: - Status tabs: Active, Expired, All
486: - Search and filter support
487: - Bindings auto-sync with MikroTik routers
488: 
489: ### Network Data Flow
490: 
491: ```mermaid
492: sequenceDiagram
493:     participant Customer
494:     participant MikroTik as MikroTik Router
495:     participant CaptivePortal as Captive Portal
496:     participant Convex as Convex Backend
497:     participant Operator as Operator Dashboard
498: 
499:     Customer->>MikroTik: Connect to WiFi
500:     MikroTik->>CaptivePortal: Redirect to captive portal
501:     CaptivePortal->>Customer: Show login/voucher page
502:     Customer->>CaptivePortal: Enter voucher code
503:     CaptivePortal->>Convex: Validate voucher
504:     Convex->>Convex: Check voucher validity, package limits
505:     Convex->>MikroTik: Authorize session (API/SSH)
506:     MikroTik->>Customer: Grant internet access
507:     Convex->>Operator: Update active sessions dashboard
508: ```
509: 
510: ### ISP Uplink Architecture
511: 
512: [[MylesNet]] operators in Uganda typically use [[Airtel]] ODU (Outdoor Unit) as their upstream internet provider. The MikroTik router handles:
513: - NAT and DHCP for the local network
514: - Bandwidth shaping per customer/package
515: - Session tracking and accounting
516: - Hotspot or PPPoE authentication
517: 
518: ### Automation Gating
519: 
520: Router automation (API calls, SSH commands, TR-069, SNMP) requires explicit [[Jonathan Myles]] approval for:
521: - Provider selection (MikroTik RouterOS API, SSH, other vendors)
522: - Credential handling (secrets must never be in plaintext vault notes, client code, or logs)
523: - API method selection
524: - Rollback plan
525: 
526: Manual network records come before automation. Phase 3 builds manual router, access point, equipment, IP pool, and health event records. Automation is Phase 4+ with provider approval.

## 1. Executive Summary

[[MylesNet]] is a multi-tenant ISP and WiFi hotspot management SaaS platform built by [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] for East African connectivity operators. It serves hotspot operators, WiFi service providers, estate network managers, hospitality venues, campus networks, community networks, and eventually larger ISP operations with a complete suite of customer management, package and voucher sales, payment processing, financial analytics, network device inventory, support ticketing, communications, and customer self-service capabilities.

### Business Context

[[Jonathan Myles]] operates a real WiFi reselling business in Uganda and Kenya. [[MylesNet]] is being built as both the operational tool for that business (dogfood/first-tenant case) and as a SaaS product for other operators. The product must work in the field -- on low-end Android phones in direct sunlight, on unreliable network connections, with mobile money as the primary payment method.

### Business Model

Subscription-based SaaS with three tiers:

| Plan | Target Operator | UGX Price | KES Price | Capability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | Single-site operator | UGX 28,000/mo | KSh 1,000/mo | One location, limited customer count, core registration, payment recording, basic analytics |
| Growth | Growing operator | UGX 78,000/mo | KSh 2,800/mo | Multiple locations, full analytics, CSV exports, SMS reminders, staff roles |
| Pro | Multi-site or franchise | UGX 196,000/mo | KSh 7,000/mo | Unlimited locations, white-label controls, API access, advanced integrations, priority support |

UGX is the primary currency (no decimal places). KES is secondary. Exact prices require [[Jonathan Myles]] confirmation before public display.

Additionally, the platform supports:
- 21-day free trial for new operators (per screenshot 00, starting at USh 25,000/month after trial)
- Referral program: 20% commission on referred operator subscription payments for 12 months (per screenshot 14)
- Voucher agent commissions and withdrawal flows

### Seven-Tier Hierarchy Fit

[[MylesNet]] fits the [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] seven-tier panel hierarchy:

| Tier | MylesNet Implementation |
|---|---|
| 1. Platform Admin | `/platform` in `apps/admin` -- [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] internal control |
| 2. Network Operator | `/admin` in `apps/network` -- ISP/hotspot operator workspace |
| 3. Operator Manager | `/admin` with elevated permissions -- regional operator oversight |
| 4. Agency Super Admin | `/admin` with agency scope -- agency client management |
| 5. Reseller Super Admin | `/admin` with reseller scope -- reseller client management |
| 6. Partner Admin | Future partner API integration tier |
| 7. Client Admin / End User | `/dashboard` in `apps/web` -- customer self-service |

### Core Values

[[MylesNet]] follows [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] M.Y.L.E.S. values:

| Letter | Value | Product Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| M | Mastery | Build reliable connectivity operations that operators can trust for revenue-critical daily work |
| Y | Youth Empowerment | Expand opportunity by helping local network operators provide better digital access to communities |
| L | Leadership | Give operators accountable controls, records, and visibility for network and customer decisions |
| E | Entrepreneurship | Support small ISP partners, resellers, and hotspot businesses with practical tools for growth |
| S | Service | Improve connectivity service delivery for customers, operators, support teams, and local communities |

## 4. Network Layer Architecture

### MikroTik Router Integration

[[MylesNet]] operators primarily use [[MikroTik]] RouterOS hardware for hotspot and PPPoE access control. The platform supports two access modes visible in screenshots 03, 04, 32, and 38:

#### Hotspot Mode (Primary)
- Captive portal authentication via voucher code or MAC-Cookie auto-reconnect
- Device remember duration configurable per tenant (default 30 days per screenshot 32)
- Auto-reconnect methods: MAC-Cookie (recommended), HTTP Cookie, or IP Binding
- Captive portal theming: template selection, background image upload, brand color override, gradient end color, font selection, and language (per screenshot 32)
- Redirect URL after successful login configurable per tenant
- Prune inactive users setting (default 30 days per screenshot 32)

#### PPPoE Mode
- PPPoE username/password authentication (screenshot 04)
- PPPoE subscription portal URL configurable per tenant (screenshot 30)
- Status tracking: Online, Offline, Active, Pending Registrations, Expired (per screenshot 04)

### IP Binding Management

Per screenshot 03, IP bindings allow specific devices to bypass hotspot authentication:
- Bind IP action creates a static binding on the linked MikroTik router
- Status tabs: Active, Expired, All
- Search and filter support
- Bindings auto-sync with MikroTik routers

### Network Data Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Customer
    participant MikroTik as MikroTik Router
    participant CaptivePortal as Captive Portal
    participant Convex as Convex Backend
    participant Operator as Operator Dashboard

    Customer->>MikroTik: Connect to WiFi
    MikroTik->>CaptivePortal: Redirect to captive portal
    CaptivePortal->>Customer: Show login/voucher page
    Customer->>CaptivePortal: Enter voucher code
    CaptivePortal->>Convex: Validate voucher
    Convex->>Convex: Check voucher validity, package limits
    Convex->>MikroTik: Authorize session (API/SSH)
    MikroTik->>Customer: Grant internet access
    Convex->>Operator: Update active sessions dashboard
```

### ISP Uplink Architecture

[[MylesNet]] operators in Uganda typically use [[Airtel]] ODU (Outdoor Unit) as their upstream internet provider. The MikroTik router handles:
- NAT and DHCP for the local network
- Bandwidth shaping per customer/package
- Session tracking and accounting
- Hotspot or PPPoE authentication

### Automation Gating

Router automation (API calls, SSH commands, TR-069, SNMP) requires explicit [[Jonathan Myles]] approval for:
- Provider selection (MikroTik RouterOS API, SSH, other vendors)
- Credential handling (secrets must never be in plaintext vault notes, client code, or logs)
- API method selection
- Rollback plan

Manual network records come before automation. Phase 3 builds manual router, access point, equipment, IP pool, and health event records. Automation is Phase 4+ with provider approval.

# Cookie Handling

[[Cookie Handling]] is mandatory for every [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] product and client project. It applies to [[WorkOS AuthKit]] sessions, tenant context, [[CSRF Protection]], onboarding state, temporary state, and any future server-set cookie.

## Cookie Security Standards

Every cookie set by a system must include all of these attributes:

- `httpOnly: true`
- `secure: true`
- `sameSite: "lax"` by default
- `path: "/"`
- `domain` explicitly set to the correct product or panel domain
- `maxAge` or `expires`

Use `sameSite: "strict"` for sensitive operations where cross-site redirects are not required.

## Never Do

- Never set a cookie without `httpOnly` unless client-side JavaScript access is explicitly required and documented in a code comment.
- Never set a cookie without `maxAge` or `expires`.
- Never store sensitive data in a cookie value. Store only a reference ID.
- Never store plaintext tokens, roles, permissions, tenant data, user data, or provider secrets in cookies.
- Never set auth cookies from client-side JavaScript.
- Never use `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` for auth tokens.
- Never set `secure: false`, including in development.
- Never use generic cookie names such as `session`, `token`, `auth`, or `user`.

## Naming Convention

Cookie names must use this format:

```text
__[product]_[purpose]
```

Examples:

- `__edumyles_session`
- `__edumyles_tenant`
- `__mylescrm_session`
- `__eduryde_session`

## Product Cookie Prefixes

| Product | Cookie prefix | Tenant domain scope | Admin panel scope | Network panel scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [[EduMyles]] | `__edumyles_` | `.edumyles.com` | `admin.edumyles.com` | `network.edumyles.com` |
| [[MylesCRM]] | `__mylescrm_` | `.mylescrm.com` | `admin.mylescrm.com` | `network.mylescrm.com` |
| [[AgriMyles]] | `__agrimyles_` | `.agrimyles.com` | `admin.agrimyles.com` | `network.agrimyles.com` |
| [[MylesCare]] | `__mylescare_` | `.mylescare.com` | `admin.mylescare.com` | `network.mylescare.com` |
| [[MylesProp]] | `__mylesprop_` | `.mylesprop.com` | `admin.mylesprop.com` | `network.mylesprop.com` |
| [[EduRyde]] | `__eduryde_` | `.eduryde.com` | `admin.eduryde.com` | `network.eduryde.com` |
| [[MylesNet]] | `__mylesnet_` | `.mylesnet.com` | `admin.mylesnet.com` | `network.mylesnet.com` |
| [[PhysioHome]] | `__physiohome_` | Not confirmed | Not confirmed | Not confirmed |
| School website clients | `__school_[slug]_` | Client domain | `admin.[domain]` (Premium) | N/A |

School website cookie rules: [[CRM/leads/School Website Technical Specification#Cookie and Consent Policy (School Sites)|School Website Technical Specification]]. Footer: [[School Website Footer Standards]].

If a final production domain differs from this table, update the relevant product decision note and this table before implementation.

## Lifetime Rules

| Cookie type | MaxAge | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Auth session through [[WorkOS AuthKit]] | 24 hours | Refreshed on activity |
| Remember me session | 30 days | Only with explicit user opt-in |
| Tenant context | Same as session | Cleared with session |
| Onboarding state | 7 days | Non-sensitive and cleared after completion |
| CSRF token | Per request | Single use and cleared immediately after use |
| Temporary state | 15 minutes | Form state or wizard progress |

## Automatic Cookie Clearing

The system must clear cookies server-side in middleware and relevant [[Next.js]] route handlers.

Required clearing events:

- Sign out: delete all `__[product]_*` cookies immediately on the server, then redirect to `/login`.
- Session expiry: clear cookies before redirecting to `/login`.
- [[WorkOS AuthKit]] role change or membership revocation: clear session cookies and force re-authentication.
- Tenant switch: clear tenant context before setting the new context.
- Password change or account deactivation: invalidate active [[WorkOS]] sessions and clear cookies across all panels.
- Master Admin and Super Admin browser close: use session cookies only with no persistence.
- Admin inactivity timeout: clear after 30 minutes of inactivity.
- Tenant app inactivity timeout: clear after 2 hours of inactivity.
- Suspicious activity: clear partial auth cookies, clear mismatched tenant cookies, clear tampered cookies, force re-authentication, and log the incident server-side.

Show a warning modal 5 minutes before inactivity expiry. On timeout, redirect to `/login` with: `Your session expired due to inactivity. Please sign in again.`

## Server-Side Clearing Pattern

Use this pattern in [[Next.js]] middleware or route handlers:

```ts
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";

const clearAuthCookies = (response: NextResponse, product: string) => {
  const cookiesToClear = [
    `__${product}_session`,
    `__${product}_tenant`,
  ];

  cookiesToClear.forEach((name) => {
    response.cookies.set(name, "", {
      httpOnly: true,
      secure: true,
      sameSite: "lax",
      path: "/",
      maxAge: 0,
      expires: new Date(0),
    });
  });

  return response;
};
```

Never use `response.cookies.delete()` alone. Always set an empty value with `maxAge: 0` and `expires: new Date(0)`.

## Cross-Subdomain Handling

For tenant subdomains such as `[tenant].[product].com`:

- Set tenant app session cookie domain to `.[product].com` when it must be shared across tenant subdomains.
- Keep tenant context specific to the current subdomain.
- Master Admin cookies must be scoped only to `admin.[product].com`.
- Super Admin cookies must be scoped only to `network.[product].com`.
- Admin and network cookies must not be valid on tenant subdomains.

## CSRF Protection

Every `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` route must use [[CSRF Protection]]:

- Generate one CSRF token per session and store it in an HttpOnly cookie.
- Require the token as a request header on every state-changing request.
- Validate the token server-side before any mutation.
- Rotate the token after every use.
- Never accept a state-changing request without a valid token.

## Cookie Audit

At the end of every session where cookies are touched, verify:

- [ ] All cookies have `httpOnly: true`.
- [ ] All cookies have `secure: true`.
- [ ] All cookies have `sameSite` set explicitly.
- [ ] All cookies have `maxAge` or `expires` set.
- [ ] Sign-out clears all cookies server-side.
- [ ] Session expiry clears all cookies server-side.
- [ ] No sensitive data is stored in cookie values.
- [ ] No generic cookie names are used.
- [ ] All cookie names are prefixed with `__[product]_`.
- [ ] Cross-subdomain scope matches product architecture.
- [ ] [[CSRF Protection]] is implemented on all mutating routes.

## Related Notes

- [[Security]]
- [[CSRF Protection]]
- [[WorkOS AuthKit]]
- [[Next.js]]
- [[Secrets And Environment Variables]]

## 6. Module Catalog

The module catalog is the union of `module-build-checklist.md`, `page-inventory.md`, and the 39-screenshot inventory. Each module lists its purpose, primary roles, key backend functions, UI routes, and dependencies.

### Users Group

#### Active Users
- **Screenshot**: `02_active_users.webp`
- **Purpose**: Real-time view of users with active vouchers, showing online/offline/all status
- **KPIs**: All Active (vouchers with active validity), Online Now (currently connected), Offline (active voucher, not connected)
- **Primary roles**: `network_operator`, `network_admin`, `customer_care`
- **Key functions**: `admin/activeUsers.list`, `admin/activeUsers.getStats`
- **Route**: `/admin/active-users`
- **Dependencies**: `customers`, `vouchers`, `accessDevices`

import { defineSchema, defineTable } from "convex/server";
import { v } from "convex/values";
import { authTables } from "@convex-dev/auth/server";

// ==========================================================================
// PHASE 1 — TENANCY & ISOLATION (X-TEN §B1, §B5)
// ==========================================================================

/**
 * Shared tenant-scope field spread into every tenant-owned table (Phase 1,
 * additive migration). Optional during the migration: existing records hold
 * `tenantId: undefined` until the gated `tenantid-backfill-001` run; once the
 * read/write-path enforcement and backfill land, enforcement flips it to
 * required. Client-supplied tenant ids are never authority.
 */
const tenantScope = {
  tenantId: v.optional(v.id("tenants")),
} as const;

export default defineSchema({
  ...authTables,

  users: defineTable({
    // Immutable identity from WorkOS. Optional while legacy Auth records are
    // migrated, then used as the sole authorization lookup key.
    workosUserId: v.optional(v.string()),
    name: v.optional(v.string()),
    image: v.optional(v.string()),
    email: v.optional(v.string()),
    emailVerificationTime: v.optional(v.number()),
    phone: v.optional(v.string()),
    phoneVerificationTime: v.optional(v.number()),
    isAnonymous: v.optional(v.boolean()),
    jobTitle: v.optional(v.string()),
    profileCompletedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
    isActive: v.optional(v.boolean()),
    deactivatedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
    platformRole: v.optional(
      v.union(
        v.literal("platform_owner"),
        v.literal("platform_admin"),
        v.literal("platform_support"),
        v.literal("agent")
      )
    ),
    // Active role assignments. Authoritative for authorization once the
    // system roles are seeded and users are backfilled. Empty/missing during
    // migration falls back to the `platformRole` mirror.
    roles: v.optional(v.array(v.id("roles"))),
    // Convex file-storage id for the account avatar (resolved to a URL on read).
    avatarStorageId: v.optional(v.string()),
    // Soft delete: removed accounts keep their row (and WorkOS user) but lose
    // all access. Restorable by trash:manage.
    deletedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
    deletedBy: v.optional(v.id("users")),
    // Persisted workspace scope for the sidebar selector (Section 30 of the
    // NOC spec): survives page refresh without browser storage.
    lastWorkspaceScope: v.optional(
      v.object({
        country: v.optional(v.string()),
        marketId: v.optional(v.id("markets")),
      })
    ),
  })
    .index("email", ["email"])
    .index("by_workosUserId", ["workosUserId"])
    .index("phone", ["phone"])
    .index("by_platformRole", ["platformRole"]),

  // ==========================================================================
  // ROLE-BASED ACCESS CONTROL
  // ==========================================================================

  /** Authoritative role registry. System roles are seeded; custom roles are synced to WorkOS (org-scoped). */
  roles: defineTable({
    name: v.string(),
    slug: v.string(),
    description: v.optional(v.string()),
    isSystem: v.boolean(),
    isPlatform: v.boolean(),
    rank: v.number(),
    permissions: v.array(v.string()),
    workosRoleId: v.optional(v.string()),
    workosRoleSlug: v.optional(v.string()),
    createdBy: v.optional(v.id("users")),
    createdAt: v.number(),
    updatedAt: v.number(),
    deletedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
    deletedBy: v.optional(v.id("users")),
  })
    .index("by_slug", ["slug"])
    .index("by_rank", ["rank"]),

  /** Mirror of WorkOS invitations (auto-joined to the platform org). */
  invitations: defineTable({
    workosInvitationId: v.string(),
    email: v.string(),
    roleId: v.optional(v.id("roles")),
    roleSlug: v.optional(v.string()),
    organizationId: v.string(),
    status: v.union(v.literal("pending"), v.literal("accepted"), v.literal("revoked")),
    invitedByUserId: v.optional(v.id("users")),
    createdAt: v.number(),
    expiresAt: v.optional(v.number()),
    acceptedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
    revokedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
  })
    .index("by_email", ["email"])
    .index("by_status", ["status"])

2:  * Pure, dependency-free helpers for WorkOS webhook signature verification.
3:  * No Convex imports so it can be unit-tested with node:test.
4:  *
5:  * WorkOS signs deliveries with an HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<raw_body>`
6:  * using the webhook endpoint's signing secret, and sends it in the
7:  * `WorkOS-Signature` header as `t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex>`.
8:  */

11: 
12: export interface WorkosSignatureParts {
13:   timestamp: number | null;
14:   signature: string | null;
15: }
16: 
17: /** Parse `t=…,v1=…` from the WorkOS-Signature header. */
18: export function parseWorkosSignatureHeader(
19:   header: string | null | undefined,
20: ): WorkosSignatureParts {
21:   if (!header) return { timestamp: null, signature: null };
22:   let timestamp: number | null = null;
23:   let signature: string | null = null;
24:   for (const part of header.split(",")) {
25:     const separator = part.indexOf("=");
26:     if (separator === -1) continue;
27:     const key = part.slice(0, separator).trim();
28:     const value = part.slice(separator + 1).trim();
29:     if (!value) continue;
30:     if (key === "t") {
31:       const parsed = Number(value);
32:       timestamp = Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed * 1000 : null;
33:     } else if (key === "v1") {
34:       signature = value;
35:     }
36:   }
37:   return { timestamp, signature };
38: }
39: 
40: export async function hmacSha256Hex(secret: string, message: string): Promise<string> {
41:   const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
42:     "raw",
43:     new TextEncoder().encode(secret),
44:     { name: "HMAC", hash: "SHA-256" },
45:     false,
46:     ["sign"],
47:   );
48:   const signature = await crypto.subtle.sign("HMAC", key, new TextEncoder().encode(message));
49:   return Array.from(new Uint8Array(signature))
50:     .map((byte) => byte.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
51:     .join("");
52: }
53: 
54: export function hexBytesEqual(leftHex: string, rightHex: string): boolean {
55:   if (leftHex.length !== rightHex.length) return false;
56:   let difference = 0;
57:   for (let index = 0; index < leftHex.length; index += 1) {
58:     difference |= (leftHex.charCodeAt(index) ^ rightHex.charCodeAt(index)) & 0xff;
59:   }
60:   return difference === 0;

11: # Role-Based UI Visibility Standards
12: 
13: [[Role-Based UI Visibility Standards]] define how [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] products show, hide, disable, and protect role-specific UI.
14: 
15: ## Shared Permissions
16: 
17: Define permissions once in a shared hook, such as `packages/ui/hooks/usePermissions.ts`. Never duplicate role checks inline across pages and components.
18: 
19: Permissions must cover:
20: - Platform admin access (organizations, networks, agencies, resellers, partners)
21: - Network operator access (network organizations, agencies, resellers)
22: - Agency client access (agency client base, billing, commissions)
23: - Reseller client access (reseller client base, territories, revenue)
24: - Partner integration access (API keys, webhooks, integration data)
25: - Tenant app access (product-specific modules, settings, reports)
26: - Finance access, data export, audit log viewing, broadcasts, billing
27: - Platform staff access, network staff access, agency staff access, reseller staff access
28: 
29: ## UI Rules
30: 
31: - Hide navigation items completely when the role has no access.
32: - Redirect immediately when the role cannot access a page.
33: - Hide action buttons when the role cannot perform the action.
34: - Disable actions instead of hiding only when the user benefits from seeing the unavailable action.
35: - Hide sensitive fields entirely for unauthorized roles.
36: - Never rely on UI hiding alone. Enforce every permission in [[Convex]] functions too.
37: - Cross-panel isolation: Agency A users never see Agency B data. Reseller A users never see Reseller B data.
38: - Partner users never see organization, network, agency, or reseller data directly.
39: 
40: ## Master Admin Sidebar
41: 
42: - Dashboard: `platform-owner`, `platform-admin`, `platform-support`
43: - Organizations: `platform-owner`, `platform-admin`
44: - Networks: `platform-owner`, `platform-admin`
45: - Agencies: `platform-owner`, `platform-admin`
46: - Resellers: `platform-owner`, `platform-admin`

# Role-Based UI Visibility Standards

[[Role-Based UI Visibility Standards]] define how [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] products show, hide, disable, and protect role-specific UI.

## Shared Permissions

Define permissions once in a shared hook, such as `packages/ui/hooks/usePermissions.ts`. Never duplicate role checks inline across pages and components.

Permissions must cover:
- Platform admin access (organizations, networks, agencies, resellers, partners)
- Network operator access (network organizations, agencies, resellers)
- Agency client access (agency client base, billing, commissions)
- Reseller client access (reseller client base, territories, revenue)
- Partner integration access (API keys, webhooks, integration data)
- Tenant app access (product-specific modules, settings, reports)
- Finance access, data export, audit log viewing, broadcasts, billing
- Platform staff access, network staff access, agency staff access, reseller staff access

## UI Rules

- Hide navigation items completely when the role has no access.
- Redirect immediately when the role cannot access a page.
- Hide action buttons when the role cannot perform the action.
- Disable actions instead of hiding only when the user benefits from seeing the unavailable action.
- Hide sensitive fields entirely for unauthorized roles.
- Never rely on UI hiding alone. Enforce every permission in [[Convex]] functions too.
- Cross-panel isolation: Agency A users never see Agency B data. Reseller A users never see Reseller B data.
- Partner users never see organization, network, agency, or reseller data directly.
