580: }
581: ```
582: 
583: <AppOnly>
584: 
585: > **Good to know:** You can configure CORS headers for individual routes in [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#cors).
586: 
587: </AppOnly>
588: 
589: ### Producing a response
590: 
591: You can respond from Proxy directly by returning a `Response` or `NextResponse` instance. (This is available since [Next.js v13.1.0](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-13-1#nextjs-advanced-proxy))
592: 
593: ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher
594: import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
595: import { isAuthenticated } from '@lib/auth'
596: 
597: // Limit the proxy to paths starting with `/api/`
598: export const config = {
599:   matcher: '/api/:function*',
600: }
601: 
602: export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
603:   // Call our authentication function to check the request
604:   if (!isAuthenticated(request)) {
605:     // Respond with JSON indicating an error message
606:     return Response.json(
607:       { success: false, message: 'authentication failed' },
608:       { status: 401 }
609:     )
610:   }
611: }
612: ```
613: 
614: ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
615: import { isAuthenticated } from '@lib/auth'
616: 
617: // Limit the proxy to paths starting with `/api/`
618: export const config = {
619:   matcher: '/api/:function*',
620: }
621: 
622: export function proxy(request) {
623:   // Call our authentication function to check the request
624:   if (!isAuthenticated(request)) {
625:     // Respond with JSON indicating an error message
626:     return Response.json(
627:       { success: false, message: 'authentication failed' },
628:       { status: 401 }
629:     )
630:   }
631: }
632: ```
633: 
634: ### Negative matching
635: 
636: The `matcher` config allows full regex so matching like negative lookaheads or character matching is supported. An example of a negative lookahead to match all except specific paths can be seen here:
637: 
638: ```js filename="proxy.js"
639: export const config = {
640:   matcher: [
641:     /*
642:      * Match all request paths except for the ones starting with:
643:      * - api (API routes)
644:      * - _next/static (static files)
645:      * - _next/image (image optimization files)
646:      * - favicon.ico, sitemap.xml, robots.txt (metadata files)
647:      */
648:     '/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|sitemap.xml|robots.txt).*)',
649:   ],
650: }
651: ```
652: 
653: You can also bypass Proxy for certain requests by using the `missing` or `has` arrays, or a combination of both:
654: 
655: ```js filename="proxy.js"
656: export const config = {
657:   matcher: [
658:     /*
659:      * Match all request paths except for the ones starting with:
660:      * - api (API routes)
661:      * - _next/static (static files)
662:      * - _next/image (image optimization files)
663:      * - favicon.ico, sitemap.xml, robots.txt (metadata files)
664:      */
665:     {
666:       source:
667:         '/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|sitemap.xml|robots.txt).*)',
668:       missing: [
669:         { type: 'header', key: 'next-router-prefetch' },
670:         { type: 'header', key: 'purpose', value: 'prefetch' },
671:       ],
672:     },
673: 
674:     {
675:       source:
676:         '/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|sitemap.xml|robots.txt).*)',
677:       has: [
678:         { type: 'header', key: 'next-router-prefetch' },
679:         { type: 'header', key: 'purpose', value: 'prefetch' },
680:       ],
681:     },
682: 
683:     {
684:       source:
685:         '/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|sitemap.xml|robots.txt).*)',
686:       has: [{ type: 'header', key: 'x-present' }],
687:       missing: [{ type: 'header', key: 'x-missing', value: 'prefetch' }],
688:     },
689:   ],
690: }
691: ```
692: 
693: > **Good to know**:
694: >
695: > Even when `_next/data` is excluded in a negative matcher pattern, proxy will still be invoked for `_next/data` routes. This is intentional behavior to prevent accidental security issues where you might protect a page but forget to protect the corresponding data route.
696: 
697: ```js filename="proxy.js"
698: export const config = {
699:   matcher:
700:     '/((?!api|_next/data|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|sitemap.xml|robots.txt).*)',
701: }
702: 
703: // Proxy will still run for /_next/data/* routes despite being excluded
704: ```
705: 
706: ### `waitUntil` and `NextFetchEvent`
707: 
708: The `NextFetchEvent` object extends the native [`FetchEvent`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FetchEvent) object, and includes the [`waitUntil()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/ExtendableEvent/waitUntil) method.
709: 
710: The `waitUntil()` method takes a promise as an argument, and extends the lifetime of the Proxy until the promise settles. This is useful for performing work in the background.
711: 
712: ```ts filename="proxy.ts"
713: import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
714: import type { NextFetchEvent, NextRequest } from 'next/server'
715: 
716: export function proxy(req: NextRequest, event: NextFetchEvent) {
717:   event.waitUntil(
718:     fetch('https://my-analytics-platform.com', {
719:       method: 'POST',
720:       body: JSON.stringify({ pathname: req.nextUrl.pathname }),
721:     })
722:   )
723: 
724:   return NextResponse.next()
725: }
726: ```
727: 
728: ### Unit testing (experimental)
729: 
730: Starting in Next.js 15.1, the `next/experimental/testing/server` package contains utilities to help unit test proxy files. Unit testing proxy can help ensure that it's only run on desired paths and that custom routing logic works as intended before code reaches production.
731: 
732: The `unstable_doesProxyMatch` function can be used to assert whether proxy will run for the provided URL, headers, and cookies.
733: 
734: ```js
735: import { unstable_doesProxyMatch } from 'next/experimental/testing/server'
736: 
737: expect(
738:   unstable_doesProxyMatch({
739:     config,
740:     nextConfig,
741:     url: '/test',
742:   })
743: ).toEqual(false)
744: ```
745: 
746: The entire proxy function can also be tested.
747: 
748: ```js
749: import { isRewrite, getRewrittenUrl } from 'next/experimental/testing/server'
750: 
751: const request = new NextRequest('https://nextjs.org/docs')
752: const response = await proxy(request)
753: expect(isRewrite(response)).toEqual(true)
754: expect(getRewrittenUrl(response)).toEqual('https://other-domain.com/docs')
755: // getRedirectUrl could also be used if the response were a redirect
756: ```
757: 
758: ## Platform support
759: 
760: | Deployment Option                                                   | Supported         |
761: | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
762: | [Node.js server](/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#nodejs-server) | Yes               |
763: | [Docker container](/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#docker)      | Yes               |
764: | [Static export](/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#static-export)  | No                |
765: | [Adapters](/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#adapters)            | Platform-specific |
766: 
767: Learn how to [configure Proxy](/docs/app/guides/self-hosting#proxy) when self-hosting Next.js.
768: 
769: ## Migration to Proxy
770: 
771: ### Why the Change
772: 
773: The reason behind the renaming of `middleware` is that the term "middleware" can often be confused with Express.js middleware, leading to a misinterpretation of its purpose. Also, Middleware is highly capable, so it may encourage the usage; however, this feature is recommended to be used as a last resort.
774: 
775: Next.js is moving forward to provide better APIs with better ergonomics so that developers can achieve their goals without Middleware. This is the reason behind the renaming of `middleware`.
776: 
777: ### Why "Proxy"
778: 
779: The name Proxy clarifies what Middleware is capable of. The term "proxy" implies a network boundary in front of the app, which is how this feature behaves. It can run outside of your application’s main runtime and handle requests before they reach your app. These characteristics align better with the term "proxy" and provide a clearer purpose for the feature.
780: 
781: ### How to Migrate
782: 
783: We recommend users avoid relying on Middleware unless no other options exist. Our goal is to give them APIs with better ergonomics so they can achieve their goals without Middleware.
784: 
785: The term “middleware” often confuses users with Express.js middleware, which can encourage misuse. To clarify our direction, we are renaming the file convention to “proxy.” This highlights that we are moving away from Middleware, breaking down its overloaded features, and making the Proxy clear in its purpose.
786: 
787: Next.js provides a codemod to migrate from `middleware.ts` to `proxy.ts`. You can run the following command to migrate:
788: 
789: ```bash
790: npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .
791: ```
792: 
793: The codemod will rename the file and the function name from `middleware` to `proxy`.
794: 
795: ```diff
796: // middleware.ts -> proxy.ts
797: 
798: - export function middleware() {
799: + export function proxy() {
800: ```
801: 
802: ## Version history
803: 
804: | Version   | Changes                                                                                       |
805: | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
806: | `v16.0.0` | Middleware is deprecated and renamed to Proxy. Proxy defaults to the Node.js runtime          |
807: | `v15.5.0` | Middleware can now use the Node.js runtime (stable)                                           |
808: | `v15.2.0` | Middleware can now use the Node.js runtime (experimental)                                     |
809: | `v13.1.0` | Advanced Middleware flags added                                                               |
810: | `v13.0.0` | Middleware can modify request headers, response headers, and send responses                   |
811: | `v12.2.0` | Middleware is stable, please see the [upgrade guide](/docs/messages/middleware-upgrade-guide) |
812: | `v12.0.9` | Enforce absolute URLs in Edge Runtime ([PR](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/33410))    |
813: | `v12.0.0` | Middleware (Beta) added                                                                       |

> **Note**: The `middleware` file convention is deprecated and has been renamed to `proxy`. See [Migration to Proxy](#migration-to-proxy) for more details.

The `proxy.js|ts` file is used to write [Proxy](/docs/app/getting-started/proxy) and run code on the server before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.

Proxy executes before routes are rendered. It's particularly useful for implementing custom server-side logic like authentication, logging, or handling redirects.

> **Good to know**:
>
> Proxy is meant to be invoked separately of your render code and in optimized cases deployed to your CDN for fast redirect/rewrite handling, you should not attempt relying on shared modules or globals.
>

It involves creating, storing, refreshing, and deleting sessions or tokens. 522: 523: There are two types of sessions: 524: 525: 1. [**Stateless**](#stateless-sessions): Session data (or a token) is stored in the browser's cookies. The cookie is sent with each request, allowing the session to be verified on the server. This method is simpler, but can be less secure if not implemented correctly. 526: 2. [**Database**](#database-sessions): Session data is stored in a database, with the user's browser only receiving the encrypted session ID. This method is more secure, but can be complex and use more server resources. 527: 528: > **Good to know:** While you can use either method, or both, we recommend using a session management library such as [iron-session](https://github.com/vvo/iron-session) or [Jose](https://github.com/panva/jose). 529: 530: ### Stateless Sessions 531: 532: 533: 534: To create and manage stateless sessions, there are a few steps you need to follow: 535: 536: 1. Generate a secret key, which will be used to sign your session, and store it as an [environment variable](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables). 537: 2. Write logic to encrypt/decrypt session data using a session management library. 538: 3. Manage cookies using the Next.js [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) API. 539: 540: In addition to the above, consider adding functionality to [update (or refresh)](#updating-or-refreshing-sessions) the session when the user returns to the application, and [delete](#deleting-the-session) the session when the user logs out. 541: 542: > **Good to know:** Check if your [auth library](#auth-libraries) includes session management. 543: 544: #### 1. Generating a secret key 545: 546: There are a few ways you can generate secret key to sign your session. For example, you may choose to use the `openssl` command in your terminal: 547: 548: ```bash filename="terminal" 549: openssl rand -base64 32 550: ``` 551: 552: This command generates a 32-character random string that you can use as your secret key and store in your [environment variables file](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables): 553: 554: ```bash filename=".env" 555: SESSION_SECRET=your_secret_key 556: ``` 557: 558: You can then reference this key in your session management logic: 559: 560: ```js filename="app/lib/session.js" 561: const secretKey = process.env.SESSION_SECRET 562: ``` 563: 564: #### 2. Encrypting and decrypting sessions 565: 566: Next, you can use your preferred [session management library](#session-management-libraries) to encrypt and decrypt sessions. Continuing from the previous example, we'll use [Jose](https://www.npmjs.com/package/jose) and React's [`server-only`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/server-only) package to ensure that your session management logic is only executed on the server. 567: 568: ```tsx filename="app/lib/session.ts" switcher 569: import 'server-only' 570: import { SignJWT, jwtVerify } from 'jose' 571: import { SessionPayload } from '@/app/lib/definitions' 572: 573: const secretKey = process.env.SESSION_SECRET 574: const encodedKey = new TextEncoder().encode(secretKey) 575: 576: export async function encrypt(payload: SessionPayload) { 577: return new SignJWT(payload) 578: .setProtectedHeader({ alg: 'HS256' }) 579: .setIssuedAt() 580: .setExpirationTime('7d') 581: .sign(encodedKey) 582: } 583: 584: export async function decrypt(session: string | undefined = '') { 585: try { 586: const { payload } = await jwtVerify(session, encodedKey, { 587: algorithms: ['HS256'], 588: }) 589: return payload 590: } catch (error) { 591: console.log('Failed to verify session') 592: } 593: } 594: ``` 595: 596: ```jsx filename="app/lib/session.js" switcher 597: import 'server-only' 598: import { SignJWT, jwtVerify } from 'jose' 599: 600: const secretKey = process.env.SESSION_SECRET 601: const encodedKey = new TextEncoder().encode(secretKey) 602: 603: export async function encrypt(payload) { 604: return new SignJWT(payload) 605: .setProtectedHeader({ alg: 'HS256' }) 606: .setIssuedAt() 607: .setExpirationTime('7d') 608: .sign(encodedKey) 609: } 610: 611: export async function decrypt(session) { 612: try { 613: const { payload } = await jwtVerify(session, encodedKey, { 614: algorithms: ['HS256'], 615: }) 616: return payload 617: } catch (error) { 618: console.log('Failed to verify session') 619: } 620: } 621: ``` 622: 623: > **Tips**: 624: > 625: > - The payload should contain the **minimum**, unique user data that'll be used in subsequent requests, such as the user's ID, role, etc. It should not contain personally identifiable information like phone number, email address, credit card information, etc, or sensitive data like passwords. 626: 627: #### 3. Setting cookies (recommended options) 628: 629: To store the session in a cookie, use the Next.js [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) API. The cookie should be set on the server, and include the recommended options: 630: 631: - **HttpOnly**: Prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing the cookie. 632: - **Secure**: Use https to send the cookie. 633: - **SameSite**: Specify whether the cookie can be sent with cross-site requests. 634: - **Max-Age or Expires**: Delete the cookie after a certain period. 635: - **Path**: Define the URL path for the cookie. 636: 637: Please refer to [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies) for more information on each of these options. 638: 639: ```ts filename="app/lib/session.ts" switcher 640: import 'server-only' 641: import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 642: 643: export async function createSession(userId: string) { 644: const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) 645: const session = await encrypt({ userId, expiresAt }) 646: const cookieStore = await cookies() 647: 648: cookieStore.set('session', session, { 649: httpOnly: true, 650: secure: true, 651: expires: expiresAt, 652: sameSite: 'lax', 653: path: '/', 654: }) 655: } 656: ``` 657: 658: ```js filename="app/lib/session.js" switcher 659: import 'server-only' 660: import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 661: 662: export async function createSession(userId) { 663: const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) 664: const session = await encrypt({ userId, expiresAt }) 665: const cookieStore = await cookies() 666: 667: cookieStore.set('session', session, { 668: httpOnly: true, 669: secure: true, 670: expires: expiresAt, 671: sameSite: 'lax', 672: path: '/', 673: }) 674: } 675: ``` 676: 677: Back in your Server Action, you can invoke the `createSession()` function, and use the [`redirect()`](/docs/app/guides/redirecting) API to redirect the user to the appropriate page: 678: 679: ```ts filename="app/actions/auth.ts" switcher 680: import { createSession } from '@/app/lib/session' 681: 682: export async function signup(state: FormState, formData: FormData) { 683: // Previous steps: 684: // 1. These checks are useful for quick operations, such as showing/hiding UI elements or redirecting users based on permissions or roles. 1018: 2. **Secure**: Checks if the user is authorized to access a route or perform an action using the session data stored in the database. These checks are more secure and are used for operations that require access to sensitive data or actions. 1019: 1020: For both cases, we recommend: 1021: 1022: - Creating a [Data Access Layer](#creating-a-data-access-layer-dal) to centralize your authorization logic 1023: - Using [Data Transfer Objects (DTO)](#using-data-transfer-objects-dto) to only return the necessary data 1024: - Optionally use [Proxy](#optimistic-checks-with-proxy-optional) to perform optimistic checks. 1025: 1026: ### Optimistic checks with Proxy (Optional) 1027: 1028: There are some cases where you may want to use [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) and redirect users based on permissions: 1029: 1030: - To perform optimistic checks. ---
title: How to implement authentication in Next.js
nav_title: Authentication
description: Learn how to implement authentication in your Next.js application.
---

Understanding authentication is crucial for protecting your application's data. This page will guide you through what React and Next.js features to use to implement auth.

Before starting, it helps to break down the process into three concepts:

1. **[Authentication](#authentication)**: Verifies if the user is who they say they are. It requires the user to prove their identity with something they have, such as a username and password.
2. **[Session Management](#session-management)**: Tracks the user's auth state across requests.
3. **[Authorization](#authorization)**: Decides what routes and data the user can access.

This diagram shows the authentication flow using React and Next.js features:

  alt="Diagram showing the authentication flow with React and Next.js features"
  srcLight="/docs/light/authentication-overview-new.png"
  srcDark="/docs/dark/authentication-overview-new.png"

# MylesNet Panel and RBAC Orientation

Quick orientation for working on MylesNet access control inside this vault. The folder's 00–12 documents are cross-product standards; MylesNet applies them through its own naming and role model.

## Canonical naming (mandatory vocabulary)
| Panel | Route | v3 name |
|---|---|---|
| Master Admin | `/platform` | Platform |
| Super Admin | `/admin` | Admin/Network |
| Tenant App | `/dashboard` | Dashboard/Tenant |
| Reseller | `/reseller` | Reseller |
| Agency / Partner | `/agency`, `/partner` | Feature-gated |

Slugs are identical in v2 and v3. `master-admin`, `super-admin`, `tenant-app`, and similar tokens are forbidden in code, routes, folders, docs, and audit records (v3 §7; Master Part C §C1).

## Where each layer is defined
| Topic | Location |
|---|---|
| Full MylesNet spec (roles, RBAC, panels, reconciliation) | [[products/mylesnet/MylesNet_Master_Technical_Specification_v3|MylesNet Master Technical Specification - Version 3 Final]] - Part A §2 personas/roles, Part B §B15 RBAC scope, Part C §C1/C2 maps |
| Cross-product panel hierarchy (7-tier) | [[architecture/rbac-panel-hierarchy/01-complete-panel-hierarchy|Complete panel hierarchy]] |
| Cross-product field-level permission matrix | [[architecture/rbac-panel-hierarchy/02-rbac-complete-reference|RBAC complete reference]] |
| Product-specific role/permission matrix | [[company-documents/product-technical/mylesnet-role-permission-matrix|MylesNet Role Permission Matrix]] |
| Convex schema + RBAC enforcement | [[architecture/rbac-panel-hierarchy/03-convex-schema-with-rbac|Convex schema with RBAC]] |
| Routing-layer enforcement | [[architecture/rbac-panel-hierarchy/04-nextjs-middleware-routing-with-rbac|Next.js middleware routing with RBAC]] |
| WorkOS configuration | [[architecture/rbac-panel-hierarchy/05-workos-configuration-with-rbac|WorkOS configuration with RBAC]] |

## MylesNet role namespaces
Three WorkOS organization scopes, then Convex for detailed grants:
1. **Platform organization** (MylesCorp): `platform-owner`, `platform-admin`, `platform-support`. No tenant data.
2. **Network organization** (MylesNet infra): `network-owner`, `network-admin`, `network-operator`. Shared RADIUS, NAS trust, connectors, workers, accounting, health.
3. **Tenant organizations** (each ISP): `tenant-admin`, `NOC`, `finance`, `sales`, `viewer`; v2 granular roles (`network-engineer`, `customer-care`, `support-agent`, `technician`, `installer`, `operator_manager`) exist as custom tenant roles. `customer` lives in a separate subscriber application.

Framework rule: WorkOS carries membership + baseline role; Convex owns permissions, site/market scope, module entitlements, support grants, and operation-level authorization. Checks are always server-side and action-specific (`tenants.manage`, `radius.coa`, `payments.reconcile`, …). Reseller access is tenant-delegated, never panel-implied.

## WorkOS environments
MylesNet sandbox environment `client_01KW2CDMPAS1H8FD68QQWY6713` / `environment_01KW2CDM74D4ZK4G89PFM92KF6`; Platform org `org_01KWQ9Q1T5WKX4KEDWPVJ395Y4`; Network org `org_01KWQ9Q6XPN5Z0MRXCTMGR94X4`. Verify live values against the Master Final Document Control before relying on them.

## Work flow reminders
- Never call a write/network mutation from MCP tools without operator confirmation; "pending_confirmation" means approved-pending in the billing app, not executed.
- Naming checks belong in every PR/review: forbidden tokens and the canonical panel vocabulary above.
- Keep this orientation in sync with the Master Final's Part A annotations and Part C reconciliation.

I now have all the technical facts I need to plan the work:

**Available AuthKit APIs:** `authkitMiddleware`, `handleAuth`, `getSignInUrl`, `getSignUpUrl`, `signOut`, `switchToOrganization`, `getWorkOS`, `getTokenClaims`, `checkRecentAuth`, `refreshSession`, `saveSession`, `withAuth`, `getSessionFromCookie`, `validateApiKey`.

The `authkitMiddleware` has `middlewareAuth: { enabled, unauthenticatedPaths, signUpPaths }`. AuthKit middleware handles session cookie `wos-session`, PKCE for callback, redirects to sign-in for unauthenticated paths.

Now, let me plan the concrete implementation. The scope is "authentication end-to-end" for MylesNet with RBAC, plus repo ↔ vault sync.

Given what exists already, the real remaining work in the CURRENT single-app reality:

### Layer 1: Proxy (routing layer) — `apps/web/proxy.ts`
- Currently delegates entirely to `authkitMiddleware`.
- I will extend it to add, **critically**, RBAC-aware optimizations that the current single-app can enforce. But RBAC needs role info in the cookie. AuthKit middleware decrypts the session cookie and can read the user. The `Session` object contains `user` with roles? Actually AuthKit session contains `user` plus claims in access token. The JWT `role` claim is emitted per workos.ts. But the middleware helper `authkitMiddleware` already returns a processed response; the wrapped proxy can't easily read user... Actually `getSessionFromCookie(request)` exists! I can call it in proxy to read the session (but that may be a double-decrypt; acceptable though the docs say avoid DB checks; cookie decrypt is fine but it does network? No - it just decrypts the signed cookie). Hmm, decrypting the session cookie in the proxy is exactly "optimistic check" pattern the Next docs recommend.

But is it safe to call `getSessionFromCookie` in proxy? It's exported and takes `NextRequest`. It presumably reads the WORKOS_COOKIE_NAME from the request cookies and decrypts with cookie password. Good.

Then RBAC enforcement at proxy level:
- Resolve host + path → expected panel (platform=`/platform`, admin=`/admin`, reseller, agency, tenant dl).
- But currently the app has no such route groups. So proxy RBAC would redirect to /no-access for users whose role doesn't allow areas that don't exist yet. Not meaningful yet.
- Meaningful NOW: redirect `/` (marketing) fine; ensure authenticated users hitting /signin go to /dashboard (authkitMiddleware does that automatically when enabled? It redirects already-authenticated users away from signin? The AuthKit middleware has `unauthenticatedPaths`; for authenticated users visiting those paths, behavior: it redirects to `/` default (redirectUri/middlewareAuth). Not fully sure.)

Decision: Since multi-panel route groups don't exist yet, RBAC routing enforcement that references `/platform`, `/admin`, `/reseller`, `/agency`, `/partner` is FUTURE work. I will implement the *tenant cookie + hostname resolution* in the proxy now (that serves both the current app and the captive portal), plus a defensive `/no-access` redirect hook, and document the panel routing as pending (backlog).

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider scope. There is real, valuable, non-breaking work I can complete end-to-end now:

1. **Cookie Handling** (`__mylesnet_*`) — implement `apps/web/lib/auth/cookies.ts` (server-only) exposing `MYLESNET_COOKIE_NAMES`, `cookieOptions`, `setTenantCookie`, `getTenantCookie`, `clearAuthCookies`. Per Cookie Handling.md this is a platform standard. Also used by the proxy to read/write the tenant cookie.

2. **CSRF Protection** — implement `apps/web/lib/auth/csrf.ts` (server-only): `generateCsrfToken`, `createCsrfProtection` helpers, and a `requireCsrfToken(request)` that validates the double-submit cookie+header pattern; export `CSRF_COOKIE` name (`__mylesnet_csrf`). Wire a demonstration: a `csrf` route handler or include in the callback route? The standard says enable on all POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. Given the app's mutations go through Convex (which has native CSRF abort for reverse-proxy scenarios), app-level CSRF matters for Next route handlers / server actions that invoke Convex with cookies. I can add a reusable helper + test.

3. **Tenant resolution middleware/helper** — `apps/web/lib/auth/tenant.ts`: resolve tenant slug from hostname (for captive portal subdomains) and from the `__mylesnet_tenant` cookie; proxy writes the tenant cookie from hostname; export `getResolvedTenant()` server helper.

4. **2FA enforcement** — `convex/lib/mfa.ts`: `MANDATORY_MFA_ROLES`, `requiresMandatory2FA(role)`, plus a `requireMfaEnabled` helper documented to be called in owner/admin mutations. 8: # Environment Variables with RBAC
9: 
10: **Version:** 1.0
11: **Purpose:** All RBAC-relevant environment variables, their purpose, and security considerations
12: 
13: ## Root .env.example
14: 
15: ```bash
16: # =============================================================================
17: # MYLESCORP RBAC & AUTHENTICATION ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
18: # =============================================================================
19: # This file contains all environment variables required for RBAC enforcement
20: # across all MylesCorp products. Copy this to .env.local for local development.
21: # =============================================================================
22: 
23: # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
24: # CONVEX DATABASE
25: # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
26: NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL=https://your-convex-deployment.convex.cloud
27: CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT_KEY=your-convex-deployment-key
28: 
29: # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
30: # WORKOS AUTHENTICATION
31: # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
32: WORKOS_API_KEY=sk_workos_your_api_key_here
33: WORKOS_CLIENT_ID=client_your_client_id_here

39: # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

42: SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN=.mylescorp.com
43: SESSION_TIMEOUT_PLATFORM_ADMIN=1800  # 30 minutes in seconds
44: SESSION_TIMEOUT_NETWORK_OPERATOR=3600  # 1 hour in seconds

46: 
47: # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

60:

62: AIRTEL_CLIENT_ID=your_airtel_client_id

64: 
65: # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

94: 
95: ## Per-App Environment Variables
96: 
97: ### Admin Panel (`apps/admin/.env.example`)
98: 
99: ```bash
100: # Admin panel specific overrides
101: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://admin.mylescorp.com
102: WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=https://admin.mylescorp.com/auth/callback

105:

108: ```bash
109: # Network panel specific overrides
110: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://network.mylescorp.com
111: WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=https://network.mylescorp.com/auth/callback

114:

120: WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=https://*.mylescorp.com/auth/callback
121: SESSION_TIMEOUT=7200  # 2 hours for client users
122: ```
123: 
124: ## RBAC-Critical Variables
125: 
126: ### 1. WORKOS_API_KEY
127: **Purpose:** Authenticate with WorkOS API for user management and organization operations
128: **Security Level:** CRITICAL
129: **Required:** YES
130: **Impact if Missing:** Cannot authenticate users, cannot manage roles
131: **Rotation:** Rotate quarterly or if compromised
132: **Access:** Only platform_admin and CI/CD systems
133: 
134: ### 2. WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET
135: **Purpose:** Verify WorkOS webhook signatures to prevent spoofing
136: **Security Level:** CRITICAL
137: **Required:** YES
138: **Impact if Missing:** Webhook spoofing attacks, unauthorized role changes
139: **Rotation:** Rotate immediately if suspected compromise
140: **Access:** Only platform_admin and webhook endpoint
141: 
142: ### 3. JWT_SECRET
143: **Purpose:** Sign and verify JWT session tokens
144: **Security Level:** CRITICAL
145: **Required:** YES
146: **Impact if Missing:** Cannot issue or validate sessions

# Environment Variables with RBAC

**Version:** 1.0
**Purpose:** All RBAC-relevant environment variables, their purpose, and security considerations

## Root .env.example

```bash
# =============================================================================
# MYLESCORP RBAC & AUTHENTICATION ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
# =============================================================================
# This file contains all environment variables required for RBAC enforcement
# across all MylesCorp products. Copy this to .env.local for local development.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONVEX DATABASE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL=https://your-convex-deployment.convex.cloud
CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT_KEY=your-convex-deployment-key

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WORKOS AUTHENTICATION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
WORKOS_API_KEY=sk_workos_your_api_key_here
WORKOS_CLIENT_ID=client_your_client_id_here
WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_your_webhook_secret_here
WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=https://your-product.mylescorp.com/auth/callback

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SESSION MANAGEMENT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
JWT_SECRET=your-super-secret-jwt-key-min-32-chars
CSRF_SECRET=your-super-secret-csrf-key-min-32-chars
SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN=.mylescorp.com
SESSION_TIMEOUT_PLATFORM_ADMIN=1800  # 30 minutes in seconds
SESSION_TIMEOUT_NETWORK_OPERATOR=3600  # 1 hour in seconds
SESSION_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT=7200  # 2 hours in seconds

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PAYMENT PROVIDERS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# M-Pesa (Safaricom)
MPESA_CONSUMER_KEY=your_mpesa_consumer_key
MPESA_CONSUMER_SECRET=your_mpesa_consumer_secret
MPESA_PASSKEY=your_mpesa_passkey
MPESA_SHORTCODE=174379

# Stripe
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_stripe_your_secret_key
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_stripe_your_webhook_secret
STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_stripe_your_publishable_key

# Airtel Money
AIRTEL_CLIENT_ID=your_airtel_client_id
AIRTEL_CLIENT_SECRET=your_airtel_client_secret

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# COMMUNICATION PROVIDERS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Africa's Talking (SMS)
AFRICASTALKING_USERNAME=your_africas_talking_username
AFRICASTALKING_API_KEY=your_africas_talking_api_key

# Resend (Email)
RESEND_API_KEY=re_your_resend_api_key
RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=noreply@mylescorp.com

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# INFRASTRUCTURE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
NODE_ENV=production
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://your-product.mylescorp.com

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MONITORING & LOGGING
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
SENTRY_DSN=https://your-sentry-dsn@sentry.io/project-id
LOG_LEVEL=info

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FEATURE FLAGS (Development Only)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_RBAC_SHADOW_MODE=false
NEXT_PUBLIC_RBAC_ENFORCEMENT_LEVEL=full  # full, partial, off
```

## Per-App Environment Variables

### Admin Panel (`apps/admin/.env.example`)

```bash
# Admin panel specific overrides
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://admin.mylescorp.com
WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=https://admin.mylescorp.com/auth/callback
SESSION_TIMEOUT=1800  # 30 minutes for platform_admin
```

### Network Panel (`apps/network/.env.example`)

```bash
# Network panel specific overrides
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://network.mylescorp.com
WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=https://network.mylescorp.com/auth/callback
SESSION_TIMEOUT=3600  # 1 hour for network operators
```

### Web App (`apps/web/.env.example`)

```bash
# Client portal specific overrides
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://*.mylescorp.com
WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=https://*.mylescorp.com/auth/callback
SESSION_TIMEOUT=7200  # 2 hours for client users
```

## RBAC-Critical Variables

### 1. WORKOS_API_KEY
**Purpose:** Authenticate with WorkOS API for user management and organization operations
**Security Level:** CRITICAL
**Required:** YES
**Impact if Missing:** Cannot authenticate users, cannot manage roles
**Rotation:** Rotate quarterly or if compromised
**Access:** Only platform_admin and CI/CD systems

### 2. WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET
**Purpose:** Verify WorkOS webhook signatures to prevent spoofing
**Security Level:** CRITICAL
**Required:** YES
**Impact if Missing:** Webhook spoofing attacks, unauthorized role changes
**Rotation:** Rotate immediately if suspected compromise
**Access:** Only platform_admin and webhook endpoint

### 3. JWT_SECRET
**Purpose:** Sign and verify JWT session tokens
**Security Level:** CRITICAL
**Required:** YES
**Impact if Missing:** Cannot issue or validate sessions
**Rotation:** Rotate quarterly, forces all users to re-authenticate
**Access:** Only platform_admin and application servers
**Minimum Length:** 32 characters (use cryptographically secure random string)

### 4. CSRF_SECRET
**Purpose:** Generate and verify CSRF tokens for form submissions
**Security Level:** HIGH
**Required:** YES
**Impact if Missing:** CSRF vulnerabilities in state-changing operations
**Rotation:** Rotate quarterly
**Access:** Only platform_admin and application servers
**Minimum Length:** 32 characters

### 5. SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN
**Purpose:** Set cookie domain for cross-subdomain session sharing
**Security Level:** MEDIUM
**Required:** YES (for cross-product identity)
**Impact if Missing:** Users must re-authenticate per subdomain
**Value:** `.mylescorp.com` (leading dot for wildcard)
**Security Note:** Only set if you control all subdomains

### 6. SESSION_TIMEOUT_*
**Purpose:** Configure session duration per role
**Security Level:** MEDIUM
**Required:** NO (defaults to 2 hours)
**Impact if Missing:** All roles use default timeout
**Values:**
- `SESSION_TIMEOUT_PLATFORM_ADMIN`: 1800 (30 minutes)
- `SESSION_TIMEOUT_NETWORK_OPERATOR`: 3600 (1 hour)
- `SESSION_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`: 7200 (2 hours)

## Security Considerations

### Secrets Management Best Practices

1. **Never commit secrets to git**
   - Add `.env.local` to `.gitignore`
   - Use `.env.example` for template only
   - Use git-secrets or similar hooks to prevent accidental commits

2. **Use environment-specific secrets**
   - Development: Local `.env.local`
   - Staging: Vercel Environment Variables
   - Production: Vercel Environment Variables with restricted access

3. **Principle of least privilege**
   - Only give CI/CD systems access to secrets they need
   - Use scoped API keys where available
   - Rotate secrets regularly

4. **Audit access to secrets**
   - Log who accessed which secrets
   - Review access logs monthly
   - Revoke access immediately when team members leave

5. **Secret rotation strategy**
   - JWT_SECRET: Quarterly (forces re-authentication)
   - CSRF_SECRET: Quarterly
   - WORKOS_API_KEY: Quarterly or if compromised
   - WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET: Immediately if compromised
   - Payment provider keys: Per provider policy

### Environment-Specific Configuration

**Development:**
```bash
NODE_ENV=development
NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_RBAC_SHADOW_MODE=true  # Log violations, don't block
NEXT_PUBLIC_RBAC_ENFORCEMENT_LEVEL=partial
```

**Staging:**
```bash
NODE_ENV=production
NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_RBAC_SHADOW_MODE=true  # Log violations, don't block
NEXT_PUBLIC_RBAC_ENFORCEMENT_LEVEL=full
```

**Production:**
```bash
NODE_ENV=production
NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_RBAC_SHADOW_MODE=false  # Block violations
NEXT_PUBLIC_RBAC_ENFORCEMENT_LEVEL=full
```

## Implementation Checklist

```
Phase 1: Setup
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
□ Create .env.example in root
□ Create per-app .env.example files
□ Add .env.local to .gitignore
□ Set up git-secrets hooks

Phase 2: Configure Secrets
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
□ Generate JWT_SECRET (32+ chars, cryptographically secure)
□ Generate CSRF_SECRET (32+ chars, cryptographically secure)
□ Obtain WORKOS_API_KEY from WorkOS dashboard
□ Obtain WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET from WorkOS dashboard
□ Configure payment provider keys
□ Configure communication provider keys

Phase 3: Deploy to Vercel
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
□ Add all secrets to Vercel project settings
□ Configure environment-specific values
□ Test staging deployment with staging secrets
□ Test production deployment with production secrets

Phase 4: Verify
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
□ Verify WorkOS authentication works
□ Verify session tokens are signed correctly
□ Verify CSRF protection works
□ Verify webhook signature verification works
□ Verify payment provider integrations work
□ Verify communication providers work

Phase 5: Documentation
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
□ Document secret rotation schedule
□ Document who has access to which secrets
□ Document incident response for secret compromise
□ Document secret generation process
```

## Secret Generation Commands

```bash
# Generate JWT_SECRET (32+ characters)
openssl rand -base64 32

# Generate CSRF_SECRET (32+ characters)
openssl rand -base64 32

# Generate WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET (WorkOS provides this)
# Get from WorkOS Dashboard → Webhooks → Your webhook → Secret
```

## Incident Response: Secret Compromise

If any secret is compromised:

1. **Immediate Actions**
   - Rotate the compromised secret immediately
   - Revoke old API keys (if applicable)
   - Force all user sessions to expire (JWT_SECRET rotation)
   - Enable additional monitoring for suspicious activity

2. **Investigation**
   - Determine how the compromise occurred
   - Check access logs for unauthorized usage
   - Assess impact (what data could have been accessed)
   - Document timeline and findings

3. **Recovery**
   - Deploy new secrets
   - Verify all systems work with new secrets
   - Monitor for any residual issues
   - Update security procedures to prevent recurrence

4. **Communication**
   - Notify affected users if data was exposed
   - Document incident for compliance (GDPR, etc.)
   - Review and update security policies

## Related Documentation

- [[05-workos-configuration-with-rbac.md]]: WorkOS integration details
- [[04-nextjs-middleware-routing-with-rbac.md]]: Session management
- [[10-monitoring-alerting-rbac.md]]: Security event monitoring

 /**
  * Shared tenant-scope field spread into every tenant-owned table (Phase 1,
  * additive migration). Optional during the migration: existing records hold
  * `tenantId: undefined` until the gated `tenantid-backfill-001` run; once the
  * read/write-path enforcement and backfill land, enforcement flips it to
  * required. Client-supplied tenant ids are never authority.
  */
 const tenantScope = {
   tenantId: v.optional(v.id("tenants")),
 } as const;
 
 export default defineSchema({
   ...authTables,
 
   users: defineTable({
     // Immutable identity from WorkOS. Optional while legacy Auth records are
     // migrated, then used as the sole authorization lookup key.
     workosUserId: v.optional(v.string()),
     name: v.optional(v.string()),
     image: v.optional(v.string()),
     email: v.optional(v.string()),
     emailVerificationTime: v.optional(v.number()),

     jobTitle: v.optional(v.string()),
     profileCompletedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     isActive: v.optional(v.boolean()),
     deactivatedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     // MFA compliance mirror (Security Standards; WorkOS mandatory-2FA roles).
     // Synced from WorkOS enrollment at identity reconcile time. A mandatory-2FA
     // role without a marker is non-compliant and server guards fail closed.
     mfaEnrolled: v.optional(v.boolean()),
     mfaEnrolledAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     platformRole: v.optional(
       v.union(
         v.literal("platform_owner"),
         v.literal("platform_admin"),
         v.literal("platform_support"),
         v.literal("agent")
       )
     ),
     // Active role assignments. Authoritative for authorization once the
     // system roles are seeded and users are backfilled. Empty/missing during
     // migration falls back to the `platformRole` mirror.
     roles: v.optional(v.array(v.id("roles"))),
     // Convex file-storage id for the account avatar (resolved to a URL on read).
     avatarStorageId: v.optional(v.string()),
     // Soft delete: removed accounts keep their row (and WorkOS user) but lose

     deletedAt: v.optional(v.number()),

     // Persisted workspace scope for the sidebar selector (Section 30 of the

     .index("phone", ["phone"])

   /** Authoritative role registry. System roles are seeded; custom roles are synced to WorkOS (org-scoped). */
   roles: defineTable({

       v.literal("suspended"),
       v.literal("cancelled"),
     ),
     // WorkOS per-tenant org id (three-scope model, Phase 2). The server-side
     // tenant resolver derives tenancy from this — never from the client.
     workosOrganizationId: v.optional(v.string()),
     settings: v.optional(v.any()),
     createdAt: v.number(),
     updatedAt: v.number(),
     deletedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
   })
     .index("by_slug", ["slug"])
     .index("by_status", ["status"])
     .index("by_workosOrganizationId", ["workosOrganizationId"]),
 
   // Warehouse of which workforce user belongs to which tenant (org-scoped).
   tenantMemberships: defineTable({
     userId: v.id("users"),
     tenantId: v.id("tenants"),
     // Bounded to the Phase 2 permission catalogue; free string while migrating.
     role: v.string(),
     status: v.union(v.literal("active"), v.literal("pending"), v.literal("revoked")),
     // WorkOS membership id once the per-tenant org exists (Phase 2).
     workosMembershipId: v.optional(v.string()),
     invitedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     joinedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     revokedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
   })
     .index("by_user", ["userId"])
     .index("by_tenant", ["tenantId"])
     .index("by_user_tenant", ["userId", "tenantId"]),
 
   // SaaS plan / entitlement attached to a tenant (G-TEN, Phase 3). `planId` is
   // a plan code string until the T-PLN catalogue lands.
   entitlements: defineTable({
     tenantId: v.id("tenants"),
     planId: v.string(),
     status: v.union(
       v.literal("trial"),
       v.literal("active"),
       v.literal("expired"),
       v.literal("suspended"),
     ),
     startsAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     expiresAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     trialEndsAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     createdAt: v.number(),
     updatedAt: v.number(),
   })
     .index("by_tenant", ["tenantId"]),
 
   // ==========================================================================
   // PHASE 0 — MIGRATION RUN INFRASTRUCTURE (§B2)
   // ==========================================================================
 
   // Tracks each migration as one idempotent, auditable, revertible run. A run
   // records bounded-batch progress (cursor/rowsProcessed), a rollback
   // checkpoint, the consolidated export manifest, assertion failures, and the
   // feature-flag gates that must be on before any enforcement checkpoint.
   migrationRuns: defineTable({
     // Immutable run id (e.g. "tenantid-backfill-001") shared across retries so
     // the run is idempotent even if the internal action re-runs.
     runId: v.string(),
     name: v.string(),
     tables: v.array(v.string()),
     status: v.union(
       v.literal("planned"),
       v.literal("running"),
       v.literal("completed"),
       v.literal("rolled_back"),
       v.literal("failed"),
       v.literal("cancelled"),
     ),
     // Bounded-backfill progress: the opaque cursor and rows processed so far.
     cursor: v.optional(v.string()),
     rowsProcessed: v.number(),
     // Declared rollback checkpoint for the most recent phase.
     rollbackCursor: v.optional(v.string()),
     rollbackRows: v.optional(v.number()),
     // Consolidated manifest of what the run moved / wrote, per table.
     // v.record() unavailable in Convex 1.44 — shape enforced by the runner.
     manifest: v.any(),
     // Feature-flag names that must be "on" before enforcement checkpoints.
     requiredFlags: v.array(v.string()),
     // Names of assertions that failed on the latest checkpoint (empty = green).
     failedAssertions: v.array(v.string()),
     error: v.optional(v.string()),
     startedBy: v.optional(v.id("users")),
     startedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     completedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     createdAt: v.number(),
   })
     .index("by_run_id", ["runId"])
     .index("by_status", ["status"])
     .index("by_created_at", ["createdAt"]),
 });

# MylesNet Full Production Technology Stack
## Architecture Summary

MylesNet will be a pnpm/Turborepo monorepo: Vercel hosts the web product; Convex provides tenant-aware SaaS workflows and real-time UI state; AWS Cape Town hosts the private AAA, network, data, queue, security, and observability plane. The system is sized and load-tested initially for 10,000 concurrent sessions, with a 99.95% target, RPO of 15 minutes, and RTO of four hours.

## Selected Stack

| Layer | Selected technology |
|---|---|
| Monorepo | pnpm, Turborepo, TypeScript |
| Web | Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Radix UI, React Hook Form, Zod, TanStack Table, ECharts |
| Product hosting | Vercel |
| Public edge | Cloudflare DNS, wildcard tenant subdomains, WAF, DDoS protection, rate limits |
| SaaS backend | Convex queries, mutations, actions, HTTP routes, crons, subscriptions, and database |
| Workforce identity | WorkOS/AuthKit for MylesCorp staff, tenant administrators, SSO, organization membership, and MFA |
| Subscriber identity | Auth0 with phone-OTP-first sign-in and password fallback; tenant-selected SMS providers through a validated communications adapter. Auth0 supports SMS passwordless connections and custom phone-provider configuration. [Auth0 SMS OTP](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/passwordless/authentication-methods/sms-otp) |
| AAA | FreeRADIUS 3.x, active-active containers, PPPoE and MikroTik Hotspot first |
| Network automation | Go services for RouterOS API, SNMP, SSH, provisioning, CoA/Disconnect, backups, and telemetry |
| Private runtime | AWS ECS Fargate in a private VPC |
| Transactional SaaS data | Convex: tenants, memberships, subscribers, services, invoices, entitlement workflow, support, UI read models |
| AAA and ledger data | Amazon RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ: RADIUS policy replicas, sessions, accounting, quotas, payment postings, and financial ledger |
| Cache and ephemeral state | Amazon ElastiCache Redis: OTP state, rate limits, locks, deduplication, and short-lived authorization cache |
| Durable jobs | Amazon SQS, EventBridge, dead-letter queues, retry policies |
| File storage | Convex Storage for ordinary attachments; Amazon S3 for backups, exports, KYC archives, router backups, and long-lived invoices |
| Secrets and encryption | AWS Secrets Manager, KMS, Vercel/Convex/WorkOS secret stores; no secrets in application tables |
| Payments | Safaricom Daraja adapter first; tenant-owned and MylesCorp-managed collection models; future adapters through the same contract |
| Communications | Tenant-selected SMS/email providers behind a provider adapter; OTP, payment, expiry, suspension, and reconnection templates |
| Monitoring | OpenTelemetry, CloudWatch, AWS Managed Prometheus/Grafana, Sentry |
| CI/CD and IaC | GitHub, GitHub Actions, Terraform, Docker, Dependabot/CodeQL/secret and container scanning |
| Deferred | Expo apps, PostGIS/MapLibre, TimescaleDB, ClickHouse, Temporal, advanced multi-vendor automation, GIS, and AI |

## Data, Identity, and Network Boundaries

- Every tenant-owned record carries `tenantId`; Convex guards, PostgreSQL row-level security, SQS job envelopes, S3 prefixes, NAS clients, payment credentials, and communications settings all enforce the same tenant boundary.
- Each ISP receives a WorkOS organization for workforce access. Subscribers are separate Auth0 identities and never acquire staff/network privileges from portal authentication.
- Configure Auth0 as a Convex OIDC provider with an exact issuer and audience; do not use an unsigned or audience-free custom token integration. [Convex OIDC guidance](https://docs.convex.dev/auth/advanced/custom-auth)
- Convex emits signed, idempotent provisioning jobs; only private Go workers may access routers or RADIUS secrets. Workers report verified results, while Convex updates real-time product state.
- FreeRADIUS authenticates locally from PostgreSQL policy replicas and cache so subscriber access does not depend on Convex or Vercel availability. RadSec is preferred; tightly restricted UDP RADIUS is allowed only through approved private VPN connectivity.
- Payment activation follows: verified callback → idempotency/reconciliation → PostgreSQL ledger posting → entitlement update → SQS provisioning job → RADIUS policy update → CoA/Disconnect → session verification → notification.

## Monorepo Shape

apps/
  web/                 Next.js admin, reseller, subscriber, and public web portals
  mobile/              Reserved for post-pilot Expo applications

convex/
  tenants/ auth/ subscribers/ billing/ entitlements/

220: ## Phase 6 — Launch panels, onboarding, portal (T-TNR, T-PRT, T-HOT)
221: 
222: - [ ] **Panel route restructure** — `/platform`, `/admin`, `/dashboard`, `/reseller` under canonical names; middleware scopes by panel; subscriber portal at tenant hostname (Dashboard/portal layout); Agency/Partner schema-aware, feature-flagged. (§B3, §B12)
223: - [ ] **Tenant onboarding wizard (T-TNR)** — legal name, branding, support contacts, market/site structure, tax, payment model, provider config, staff, notification prefs, service-plan catalogue, first network site; dependency status (WorkOS membership, DNS, connector, RADIUS client, payment sandbox, messaging, imports, go-live); drafts + validation + change history + approval. (§B5)
224: - [ ] **CSV onboarding imports** — templates, validation, duplicate detection, dry-run + error export, reviewer approval, idempotent run IDs, reconciliation, audit; subscribers/services/invoices/opening balances/routers/APs/agents/vouchers/historical data; recoverable or reverted as one tracked operation. (§B5)
225: - [ ] **Customer portal (T-PRT)** — mobile-first; service state + restriction reason + amount due + next action; usage/session history, invoices, receipts, verified payments, plan options, device management, contact updates, vouchers, tickets, announcements, communication prefs; never exposes staff/infra/raw accounting/secrets. (§B9)
226: - [ ] **Hotspot & captive portal (T-HOT)** — built from the canonical [[../captive-portal-specification|Captive Portal Specification]] in the standalone `captive-portal/` repo folder (core/, ui/, templates/, i18n/, config/, api/, terms/, test/) mounted as `app/(portal)/hotspot/**` route stubs + `convex/portal/` adapters. **MVP auth**: voucher, phone+SMS OTP, MAC/HTTP-cookie, IP binding. **Reconnection**: detection ladder (session/mac-cookie → registered device → phone prompt → manual fallbacks voucher/OTP/QR/credentials) with welcome-back dashboard. **Free trial**: one-time per device/phone with tenant-configurable reset window (`claim → reclaimableAt`). **Payments**: in-portal M-Pesa STK Push with `intent → callback verify → reconcile → entitlement → network job → CoA/reauth → verified connected` and application-vs-network state (`payment_confirmed / provisioning / connected / reconnection_failed`). **Branding**: template + color/logo/background/font/language overrides. **Splash**: terms + privacy + optional operator splash; no third-party ad platform in MVP. **Devices**: self-service list/rename/remove, per-plan limits. **Analytics**: core (visits, attempts, method usage, redemption, conversion, sessions). **MikroTik**: Convex-direct RouterOS API first (approval-gated automation); FreeRADIUS upstream is the Phase 7 upgrade path — this resolves the old Phase 6↔7 circular dependency (portal UI no longer depends on N-AAA being built first). (§B9, §B15)
227: 
228: ## Phase 7 — RADIUS, connectors, routers, accounting, CoA, HA (N-AAA, N-ACC, N-COA, N-RAD, N-SES, N-IP, N-WRK, N-CON, N-RT, N-LAB, T-NOC, T-SES)
229: 
230: - [ ] **FreeRADIUS package (N-AAA/N-LAB)** — `services/radius`: config, modules, dictionaries, committed fixtures (Request → Response); auth methods PAP/CHAP/MS-CHAPv2/EAP/EAP-TLS/PEAP/EAP-TTLS/MAC/cert/voucher/captive; PPPoE + Hotspot first. (§B7, §B8)
231: - [ ] **Local auth path** — authN/authZ from PostgreSQL policy replicas + Redis cache; subscriber access never depends on Convex/Vercel. (§B7, §B8)
232: - [ ] **RadSec/VPN transport (N-RAD)** — RadSec preferred; UDP only via approved VPN; per-NAS secrets with rotation; NAS client registry with `tenantId` + site scope. (§B7, §B8)
233: - [ ] **Accounting pipeline (N-ACC)** — Start/Interim/Stop, correlation, dedupe, rollover, missing-Stop, stale-session handling, NAS restarts; partitioned tenant-filtered tables; queues + DLQ. (§B7, §B16)
234: - [ ] **CoA/Disconnect (N-COA)** — controlled, rate-limited, audited, verified against live NAS/session state. (§B7, §B8)
235: - [ ] **Go network worker (N-WRK)** — RouterOS API/SNMP/SSH/provisioning/CoA/backups/telemetry; idempotent (job-id upserts), Secrets Manager at start + rotation, least-privilege IAM, dry-run + verified-completion. (§B6, §B18)
236: - [ ] **Edge connector (N-CON)** — convert existing collector to mTLS connector model: no inbound port, rotation/revocation audit, signed results. (§B6)
237: - [ ] **Router/NAS/AP onboarding (T-NOC)** — router wizard Monitoring + RADIUS-ready modes; generated templates for review (no unattended push at launch; two-person approval for high risk); AP vendor adapters (MikroTik, Ubiquiti, Cambium, TP-Link, Aruba, Ruckus) with SNMP fallback; discovery review before approval; drift/backup/health. (§B6)
238: - [ ] **IP pools & IPAM (N-IP)** — IPv4/IPv6 pools, assignments, static IPs, VLAN scoping. (§B7, §B15)
239: - [ ] **Session management (N-SES)** — active/stale/terminated/failed views, search, per-client disconnect, session history, duplicate/stale detection, per-session record fields per proposal §8. (§B7)
240: - [ ] **Usage & quotas (T-SES)** — time/data/daily/monthly/per-device/shared quotas, fair-use, rollover, warning/hard/soft limits, threshold-triggered policy change, usage surfaced in portal/invoices/reports/APIs. (§B7; proposal §9)
241: - [ ] **RADIUS lab + failover acceptance (N-LAB/X-LAB)** — PPPoE + Hotspot, RadSec/VPN, NAS restriction, accounting behaviors, stale sessions, CoA reliability, policy-version accuracy, quota enforcement, connector rotation, worker retry, active-active failover, degraded-mode. (§B19, §B14)
242: 
243: ## Phase 8 — Infrastructure, observability, API, operations (X-IAC, X-MON, X-API, X-OPS, X-FRD, T-RPT, T-EXP)
244: 
245: - [ ] **Terraform AWS foundation** — VPC/private subnets/NAT/Fargate/RDS Multi-AZ/Redis/SQS/EventBridge/DLQ/S3/Secrets Manager/KMS/Cloudflare; remote state with locking; reviewed plans. (§B8, §B12)
246: - [ ] **Resilience targets instrumented** — 99.95% availability, RPO 15 min, RTO 4 h; Cape Town primary with disclosed DR; PITR + backups + restore tests + DR drill recorded. (§B8)
247: - [ ] **Redis ephemeral plane** — OTP, rate limits, locks, dedupe, short-lived auth cache; tenant-namespaced keys; atomic ops; never system of record. (§B8)
248: - [ ] **OpenTelemetry end-to-end (X-MON)** — FreeRADIUS, Go worker, PostgreSQL, Redis, Next.js/Convex emit traces/metrics/logs (`service.name`, `tenantId`, `layer`); CloudWatch sink, managed Prom/Grafana, Sentry with tenant context redacted; signal list per Master §B13 incl. auth RPS, accounting RPS, concurrency, response time, rejection/failure rates. (§B13)
249: - [ ] **Runbooks** — tenant onboarding, WorkOS role/membership, support elevation, payment outage, RADIUS node failure, accounting backlog, connector compromise, cert rotation, router change review, provider webhook failure, data restore, security incident, planned maintenance; each: owner, evidence, escalation, rollback, post-incident review. (§B13)
250: - [ ] **Key & secret rotation live** — DB passwords, router/API creds, connector certs, collector identities rotate; workers refresh on rotation; scanning green. (§B8, §B13)
251: - [ ] **Fraud & abuse controls (X-FRD)** — detectors per Master §B12 + proposal §14; concurrent limits, MAC binding, velocity, quarantines, review queues, step-up; explainable alerts only. (§B12)
252: - [ ] **Public/partner API (X-API)** — versioned REST/OpenAPI (+ optional GraphQL), scoped machine credentials, tenant isolation, pagination/filter/sort, idempotency, rate limits, tracing, structured errors, webhooks + event subscriptions, agreed event names, SDKs. (§B18)
253: - [ ] **Administration & configuration (X-OPS)** — full config surface with drafts/validation/approval/versioning/rollback/change history/env separation. (§B15, proposal §23)
254: - [ ] **Reporting (T-RPT) + exports (T-EXP)** — full Master report list; scheduled delivery; role-scoped export. (§B11)
255: 
256: ## Phase 9 — Launch audit, load, controlled cutover
257: 
258: - [ ] **Full acceptance suite** — cross-tenant denial, payment duplicate/reversal, RADIUS failover + stale accounting, backup-restore proof, RPO/RTO drill, webhook signature tests, WorkOS sync tests, Playwright role/tenant tests, a11y, security, load. (§B14, §B19)
259: - [ ] **10,000-session load test** — concurrent RADIUS/accounting/UI mix with headroom; queue capacity + latency budgets recorded. (stack Architecture summary; §B8)
260: - [ ] **Cutover plan + supervised windows** — reconciliation, WorkOS role/membership verification, connector credential rotation, RADIUS client validation, payment-to-entitlement smoke test, monitoring, incident ownership, rollback limit, written sign-off. (§B2)
261: - [ ] **Retire global collector shared secret** — only after all connectors have validated mTLS identities. (§B2, §B6)
262: - [ ] **Final acceptance report** — environments, evidence per gate, limitations, owner sign-off; build success alone is never a release criterion. (§B14)
263: 
264: ## Deferred roadmap
265: 
266: - [ ] **Mobile & field ops (D-MOB)** — Expo admin/tech apps; reopen after pilot with measured need. (stack Deferred)
267: - [ ] **Fiber GIS + IPAM inventory (D-GIS)** — reopen after pilot. (stack Deferred)
268: - [ ] **AI (D-AI)** — reopen when data quality is stable; explainable and permissioned. (stack Deferred; Master §B12)
269: - [ ] **TimescaleDB/ClickHouse (D-TSDB)** — reopen on measured write/query evidence. (stack Deferred)
270: - [ ] **Diameter readiness (D-DIAM)** — reopen after RadSec/AAA acceptance. (proposal §1)
271: 
272: ## Continuous rules (every change)
273: 
274: - Each PR: lint, typecheck, unit/integration tests, `tokens:check`, build, tenant-isolation review, and the "only stack-listed technologies" check against [[../technology-stack|technology stack]].
275: - Move completed checkboxes to [[done]] with the same anchors; keep task lanes mutually exclusive.
276: - No payment initiation, RADIUS production traffic, direct router configuration, or provider webhooks without their contract and acceptance evidence.

Complete feature and module backlog for `mylesnet-dashboard`, sequenced by dependency, evidence gates, and the in-place transition defined in the [[../MylesNet_Master_Technical_Specification_v3|Master Technical Specification - Version 3 Final]] (Part A module catalogue §6, Part B, Part C). Every task uses only technologies from the [[../technology-stack|technology stack]].

This backlog has three parts:

1. **Module catalogue** — every core module of the system (v2 §6 modules, v3 additions §B15, and the 2026-09-09 feature proposal) with its build phase and current status.

3. **Chronological build order** — Phase 0-9 task lists; each phase names the modules it delivers.

Status legend: ● exists today in the single-tenant dashboard (must be rescoped to `tenantId` + panel), ◆ partially exists, ○ new build.

## Part 1 — Module catalogue

### Platform & grant control

| ID | Module | Core capability | Phase | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G-TEN | Tenants & Platform subscriptions | Tenant records, SaaS plan entitlements, manual SaaS invoices, payment status, suspension policy, support | 3 | ○ |
| G-ADM | Platform admin & security root | Owner-assignment protection, protected settings, global audit, change approval, platform health | 3 | ○ |

### Network panel (shared RADIUS and operations plane)

| ID | Module | Core capability | Phase | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| N-AAA | RADIUS AAA core | Auth: PAP, CHAP, MS-CHAPv2, EAP, EAP-TLS, PEAP, EAP-TTLS, MAC auth, certificate auth, voucher auth, captive-portal auth. Authorization: per-user policy, speed/VLAN/IP pool/static IP/session/data/time/device limits, schedules. PPPoE + MikroTik Hotspot first. **Phase 7; the Phase 6 captive portal does not wait on N-AAA** — it authenticates via Convex-direct RouterOS API (see [[../captive-portal-specification|Captive Portal Specification]] §24) | 7 | ○ |
| N-ACC | Accounting pipeline | Start / Interim-Update / Stop, session correlation, dedupe, counter rollover, missing-Stop, stale sessions, NAS restarts, partitioning | 7 | ○ |
| N-COA | CoA & Disconnect control | CoA / Disconnect-Request to NAS, verification, rate-limit, audit | 7 | ○ |
| N-RAD | RADIUS clients, RadSec, transport | NAS/RADIUS clients with `tenantId`, shared-secret rotation, RadSec preferred, VPN-restricted UDP | 7 | ○ |
| N-SES | Session management | Active / stale / terminated / failed views, search, disconnect, client-session CoA, session history, duplicate & stale detection | 7 | ○ |
| N-RT | Router estate & health | RouterOS, thresholds, health, telemetry, monitoring, incidents, maintenance (existing estate) | 7 | ● |
| N-WRK | Network workers (Go) | Provisioning, RouterOS API, SNMP, SSH, backups, drift, telemetry, CoA delivery; idempotent, least-privilege | 7 | ○ |
| N-CON | Edge connector / collector | Outbound connector on tenant LAN, mTLS client + server certs, rotation/revocation, no inbound port, signed results (existing collector → connector model) | 7 | ◆ |
| N-IP | IP pools & IPAM | IPv4/IPv6 pools, assignments, static IPs, VLAN scoping | 7 | ○ |
| N-LAB | AAA acceptance lab | FreeRADIUS config + dictionaries, RADIUS test fixtures, PPPoE/Hotspot lab, RadSec lab, failover lab | 7 | ○ |

### Tenant Dashboard modules (subscriber + billing + network for one ISP)

| ID | Module | Core capability | Phase | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-TNR | Tenant onboarding & readiness | Create tenant (country, tz, currency, plan, limits, hostname, first owner invite), wizard with dependency status, CSV imports, go-live approval | 6 | ○ |
| T-SUB | Subscriber CRM | Unified account (person/household/business/school/hotel/gov/wholesale/reseller), contacts, KYC, addresses + GPS, services per customer, multi-location, notes, contracts, communication history, timeline, duplicate detection, controlled merge, configurable statuses, multiple auth identities (username, MAC, SIM, cert, phone, email, ext-IDP) | 3 | ○ |
| T-SRV | Services & lifecycle automation | Auto create/modify/suspend/resume/upgrade/downgrade/terminate on payment/plan change/expiry/fraud/support/cancellation; onboarding; auto credential generation; activation after payment; scheduled activation/suspension; grace; auto reconnection; portability/username change; bulk provisioning/status; rollback on failure; approval for high-risk/enterprise | 3 | ○ |
| T-PLN | Plans & policy engine | Plan vs subscriber separation; download/upload/burst speed/duration/threshold, guaranteed BW, max sessions/devices, data caps, fair-use, priority, VLAN, IP pool, static IP, IPv4/IPv6, DNS, firewall profile, traffic class, service hours, expiry rules, quotas; residential/business/dedicated/wholesale/hotspot/night/weekend/family/student/enterprise/promotional; versioned policies | 3 | ○ |
| T-CRED | Credentials | Multiple auth identities per subscriber; reveal prohibited; reset → audited replacement + provisioning job; credential rotation | 3 | ○ |
| T-BIL | Billing | Prepaid/postpaid/hybrid; recurring invoices; prorated; taxes; discounts; coupons; promotions; deposits; credit limits; wallets; partial payments; installments; credit/debit notes; refunds; auto-reconciliation; overdue → grace → suspension | 4 | ○ |
| T-PAY | Payments & gateways | Daraja (M-Pesa) first; Airtel Money, cards, bank transfer, Pesapal, Flutterwave, PayPal, USSD, QR behind adapter wall; intent → verified callback → idempotency → posting → entitlement → job → CoA → verify → notify; full state set (initiated/pending/success/failed/reversed/refunded/disputed/reconciled); webhook verify; duplicate protection; settlement | 4 | ○ |
| T-LED | Revenue & controls | Immutable ledger postings (ISO currency + FX snapshot), MRR, daily revenue, ARPU, payment success rate, failed payments, overdue balances, churn revenue loss, plan profitability, gateway performance | 4 | ○ |
| T-VOU | Vouchers | Generate (batches, code lengths/prefix), scratch cards, QR, redeem, sale attribution, free trial, giveaways, expired sweep, voucher reuse controls (existing estate) | 4 | ● |
| T-AG | Agents, resellers & commissions | Agent/reseller accounts, delegated permissions, plan-specific pricing, price overrides, commissions, credit balances, customer ownership, settlement reports, agent dashboards (existing estate) | 4 | ● |
| T-SES | Usage & quotas | Time/data/daily/monthly/per-device/shared-family quotas, fair-use thresholds, rollover, warning thresholds, hard/soft limits, automatic policy change at threshold, usage in portal/invoices/reports/APIs | 7 | ○ |
| T-PRT | Customer self-service portal | Secure login; service status; usage history; pay bills; download invoices/receipts; change plan; manage devices; update contacts; tickets; chat; announcements; multiple services; redeem vouchers; refer friends; suspension/expiry explanations with next action | 6 | ○ |
| T-HOT | Hotspot & captive portal | Canonical scope: [[../captive-portal-specification|Captive Portal Specification]] (T-HOT). MVP: voucher + phone/SMS OTP + MAC/HTTP-cookie + IP-binding auth; multi-path reconnection + welcome-back dashboard; one-time free trial with tenant reset window; in-portal payment (M-Pesa STK Push first); sessions + self-service devices; usage/quota visibility; terms + operator splash; brand templates; SMS notifications; core analytics; MikroTik Convex-direct integration (approval-gated). Later: username/password, scratch cards, guest access, WhatsApp/social login (provider allowlist), FreeRADIUS upstream (Phase 7), ad platform | 6 | ○ |
| T-TKT | Help desk | Portal/email/WhatsApp/SMS/staff intake, categories, priorities, statuses, assignment, internal notes, attachments, SLA timers, escalation, canned responses, knowledge articles, customer history, satisfaction surveys; agent can inspect active session, test auth, disconnect, view accounting/policy context without raw credentials | 5 | ◆ |
| T-COM | Communications | SMS/email/WhatsApp/push/in-portal; templates with variables; triggers (registration, payment success/failure, invoice, expiry, suspension, reconnection, usage threshold, ticket, outage, maintenance, security); delivery status, retries, provider failover, opt-out, message history, campaign scheduling, segmentation, rate controls, consent | 4 | ◆ |
| T-NOC | Tenant network inventory | Tenant NOC manages sites, routers, NAS clients, APs, switches, uplinks, IP pools, config templates, telemetry, incidents, maintenance windows; only Platform/Admin create shared RADIUS nodes (existing estate) | 7 | ● |
| T-RPT | Reporting | Active subscribers, registrations, renewals, churn, plan performance, revenue, payment success, aging, gateway reconciliation, session usage, auth failures, NAS health, CoA success, voucher sales, commission, ticket SLA, CLV; date/region/plan/method/NAS/agent/customer-type filters; exports; scheduled delivery; role-based access | 8 | ○ |
| T-EXP | Exports & scheduled reports | Usage and report exports, scheduled report definitions, role-scoped export gate (existing estate) | 8 | ● |

### Subscriber identity & portal boundary

| ID | Module | Core capability | Phase | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-AUTH | Auth0 subscriber identity | Phone-OTP-first SMS passwordless + password fallback via tenant communications adapter; Convex OIDC with exact issuer/audience; portal-only claims, no staff/network privileges (supersedes Master §B4 old "rejected" line per 2026-09-09 stack) | 2 | ○ |

### Cross-cutting (shared by every panel)

| ID | Module | Core capability | Phase | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X-TEN | Tenancy & isolation | `tenantId` on every tenant-owned record; server-side resolver (hostname + WorkOS org); tenant guards on every query/mutation/http/job/webhook/export/storage URL; RLS; denial tests | 1 | ○ |

| X-AUD | Audit & data governance | Immutable audit (actor, action, object, previous/next value, timestamp, source IP, UA, result); retention, KYC, consent, export, deletion, residency, tenant deletion workflow | 2 | ○ |
| X-SEC | Security controls | MFA, password policy, least privilege, device trust, session expiry, login history, IP allowlists, suspicious-login, scoped API tokens, OAuth 2.0/OIDC, encryption in transit/at rest, secrets mgmt, key rotation; RADIUS IP restriction, secret rotation, request signing, replay protection, rate limits, brute-force detection, lockout, enumeration protection | 2 | ○ |
| X-FRD | Fraud & abuse | Impossible travel, excessive concurrent sessions, credential sharing, repeated auth failure, unusual data, suspicious payments, repeated voucher use, MAC churn, abnormal NAS, account-takeover indicators; concurrent limits, MAC binding, device fingerprinting, velocity limits, voucher restrictions, IP reputation, quarantine, review queues, risk-based step-up; explainable alerts, no silent auto-block | 8 | ○ |
| X-API | Public/partner API + webhooks | Versioned REST + OpenAPI, optional GraphQL; auth, subscribers, services, plans, sessions, devices, invoices, payments, vouchers, tickets, notifications, reports, config; OAuth 2.0, scoped API keys, RBAC, tenant isolation, pagination/filtering/sort, idempotency, rate limits, tracing, structured errors, webhooks, event subscriptions, SDKs; agreed event names | 8 | ○ |
| X-MON | Monitoring & observability | Auth success/rejection/latency/timeout; accounting loss; CoA success; NAS availability; sessions; bandwidth; interface health; drill-through; dashboards with thresholds, alert routing, incident history, maintenance windows, log aggregation, Syslog, SNMP, NetFlow/sFlow; auth/session metrics (RPS, concurrency, response time, rejection %, failure %) | 8 | ○ |
| X-OPS | Administration & configuration | Organizations, branches, currencies, taxes, time zones, languages, brands, payment gateways, SMS/WhatsApp/email providers, RADIUS clients, NAS, IP pools, VLANs, plans, notification templates, roles, permissions, audit retention, backup schedules, feature flags; validation, drafts, approval, versioning, rollback, change history, dev/staging/prod separation | 8 | ○ |
| X-IAC | Infrastructure, backup & DR | Terraform (VPC, ECS Fargate, RDS Multi-AZ, Redis, SQS/EventBridge/DLQ, S3, Secrets Manager, KMS, Cloudflare); encrypted backups, PITR, replication, config exports, retention, restore tests, DR runbooks | 8 | ○ |
| X-LAB | Quality gates | Unit, integration, WorkOS webhook/membership, contractor, RADIUS lab, failure injection, Playwright, a11y, security, load, restore, DR tests; cross-tenant denial is a release gate | 1-9 | ○ |

### Deferred (reopen only with measured need — stack + Master §B12)

| ID | Module | Core capability | Reopen gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-MOB | Admin & technician mobile (Expo) | Dashboards, alerts, lookup, ticket actions, payments; work orders, GPS, photos, signatures, inventory, install checklists, offline with encrypted local storage + explicit sync + remote wipe | After AAA/billing pilot |
| D-GIS | Fiber GIS, IPAM, inventory | Network mapping, IP management, asset inventory | After pilot |

## Phase 0 — Governance, environment, transition inventory
