## Phase 1 — Tenant schema and data isolation (X-TEN)

**Status: ACTIVE (2026-09-11) — first-order development step for Week 1**

- [ ] **Tenant/org/entitlement tables in Convex** — `tenants`, tenant `memberships`, `entitlements`, `tenantId` on every tenant-owned document, composite indexes. (§B1, §B5)
- [ ] **Tenant-resolution helper layer** — server derives tenant from hostname + WorkOS org; required on every query/mutation/http route; client-supplied `tenantId` is never authority. (§B1, §B5)
- [ ] **Cross-cutting tenant contracts** — audit keys, object-storage keys (tenant-prefixed), queue-job envelopes, webhook mapping, import/export run IDs all carry `tenantId`. (§B2, §B16, §B18)
- [ ] **Additive `tenantId` migration of the existing schema** — staged backfill per inventory class; read-path enforcement before write-path enforcement. (§B2)
- [ ] **Market/site re-scoping** — markets → tenant sites; market memberships, financials, telemetry, Centipid mirrors relabelled and reconciled. (§B2, §B16)
- [ ] **PostgreSQL foundation** — RDS Multi-AZ (Terraform), RLS-enabled schema for AAA/ledger, service-account boundary, `SET app.tenant_id` rule. (§B1, §B8, §B12)
- [ ] **Isolation test suite** — cross-tenant denial is a release gate; run in CI and record in acceptance report. (§B14, §B19)

## Phase 2 — Identity, RBAC, subscriber identity (X-RBAC, S-AUTH, X-SEC, X-AUD)

- [ ] **Three-scope WorkOS model** — Platform, Network, one org per tenant via [[WorkOS MCP]]; webhook maps known orgs only, quarantines unknown events. (§B4)
- [ ] **Permission catalog converged to the Master list** — `tenants.manage`, `memberships.manage`, `subscribers.read/manage`, `services.manage`, `policies.manage`, `sessions.read/disconnect`, `radius.coa`, `devices.read/manage`, `connector.manage`, `invoices.read/manage`, `payments.reconcile`, `vouchers.issue`, `tickets.manage`, `communications.send`, `reports.export`, `audit.read`, `security.manage`, `support.grant`; custom tenant roles bounded to catalog with immutable slugs. (§B15)
- [ ] **Auth0 subscriber identity** — Convex OIDC exact issuer/audience; phone-OTP-first SMS passwordless + password fallback via tenant communications adapter; portal-only claims. (stack Subscriber identity; supersedes §B4 old Auth0-rejection line)
- [ ] **Secure sessions + CSRF** — rotation, revocation on deactivation, cookie attributes, CSRF protection, no session reuse as API credential. (§B8, §B4)
- [ ] **Support grants** — time-bound, reason-coded, audited; no permanent tenant membership for staff. (§B4, §B17)
- [ ] **Audit event contract (X-AUD)** — immutable events with actor, action, object, before/after, timestamp, source IP, UA, result; tenant-scoped. (§B13, §B16)
- [ ] **Authorization + negative tests** — hidden-mutation denial, role visibility, disabled user, cross-tenant actor. (§B19)

## Phase 3 — Core tenant, subscriber, service, policy, audit (G-TEN, T-SUB, T-SRV, T-PLN, T-CRED)

- [ ] **Tenant provisioning state machine** — commercial approval → tenant + entitlement → WorkOS org link → owner invitation → hostname → readiness checklist → audit → onboarding comms; no orphan active tenant. (§B5, §B17)
- [ ] **Subscriber CRM (T-SUB)** — unified account model, contacts, KYC, addresses + GPS, multi-service, multi-location, notes, contracts, timeline, duplicate detection, controlled merge, configurable statuses, multiple auth identities per subscriber. (§B9)
- [ ] **Service lifecycle (T-SRV)** — draft → pending activation → active → grace → suspended → expired → blocked → terminated → reconnection pending → failed provisioning; durable events; explicit retry/rollback; bulk provisioning/status; approval for high-risk changes. (§B9, §B17)
- [ ] **Plans & policy engine (T-PLN)** — plan vs subscriber separation; full policy attribute set (speed/burst, sessions/devices, data/time quotas, priority, VLAN, IP pool, static IP, IPv4/IPv6, DNS, firewall, service hours, expiry, usage quotas); plan verticals; versioned policies so history stays accurate. (§B7, §B15)
- [ ] **Credential management (T-CRED)** — reveal prohibited, reset → audited replacement + provisioning job, rotation. (§B7, §B15)
- [ ] **Platform tenant & subscription module (G-TEN)** — tenant subscription, plan entitlements, manual SaaS invoices, payment status, suspension policy, support. (§B10)

## Phase 4 — Payments, ledger, notifications (T-BIL, T-PAY, T-LED, T-VOU, T-AG, T-COM)

- [ ] **Payment intent + activation state machine (T-PAY)** — pending → verified callback/status → amount/currency/tenant/reference/idempotency validation → posting → reconciliation → entitlement → network job → CoA (Phase 7) → verify → receipt+notify; duplicate/delayed/reversed/disputed/mismatched = explicit exceptions, never double-activate. (§B10, §B17)
- [ ] **Immutable financial ledger (T-LED)** — append-only postings, ISO currency + FX snapshot, compensating entries, finance-grade controls; in PostgreSQL with RLS. (§B10, §B16)
- [ ] **Daraja adapter (sandbox)** — STK Push, signature-verified callbacks, M-Pesa transaction-id dedupe, reconciliation pulls, reversal/dispute states; merchant authorization + contract + fraud controls before production. (§B10)
- [ ] **Provider adapter wall** — Airtel Money, cards, bank, Pesapal, Flutterwave, PayPal, USSD, QR via same idempotent contract after approval. (§B10)
- [ ] **Billing (T-BIL)** — prepaid/postpaid/hybrid, recurring invoices, prorating, taxes, discounts, coupons, deposits, credit limits, wallets, partial payments, installments, credit/debit notes, refunds, auto-reconciliation; overdue → grace → suspension; SaaS billing separated from ISP subscriber billing. (§B10)
- [ ] **Vouchers (T-VOU)** — generate batches, scratch cards, QR, redeem, free trial, giveaways, expired sweep, reuse controls. (§B15; existing estate rescoped)
- [ ] **Agents/resellers (T-AG)** — delegated permissions, pricing overrides, commissions, credit balances, settlement reports, agent dashboards. (§B15; existing estate rescoped)
- [ ] **Communications adapter (T-COM)** — SMS/email/WhatsApp/push/in-portal; templates + triggers; delivery status/retries/failover/opt-out/campaigns/segmentation/rate controls/consent; Auth0 OTP SMS routes through the tenant adapter. (§B11)
- [ ] **Signed idempotent webhooks (X-API foundations)** — signature verify, dedupe, retry, DLQ; unknown mappings quarantined. (§B18)

## Phase 5 — Shared UI and panel contracts

Delivers: panel shell, shared packages, help desk baseline (T-TKT).

- [ ] **Shared packages** — `packages/ui` (shadcn/ui + Radix), `packages/schemas` (Zod), `packages/api-contracts` (versioned, OpenAPI-derived), `packages/config`; UI/API divergence blocked at type level. (§B12)
- [ ] **Panel shell architecture** — Platform/Admin/Dashboard/reseller nav + route namespaces per panel map; shared layout/table/form/metric/chart components; ECharts lazy-loaded; TanStack Table. (§B3, §B12)
- [ ] **Design-token completion** — migrate residual raw literals to semantic/component tokens as components change; tenant brand confined to Dashboard/portal. (design/tokens v2.0)
- [ ] **Help desk baseline (T-TKT)** — ticket intake (portal/email/SMS/WhatsApp/staff), categories, priorities, assignment, internal notes, attachments, SLA timers, escalation, canned responses, knowledge articles, customer history, satisfaction surveys; agent session/auth/accounting context without raw credentials. (§B11; existing tickets estate rescoped)

## Phase 6 — Launch panels, onboarding, portal (T-TNR, T-PRT, T-HOT)

- [ ] **Panel route restructure** — `/platform`, `/admin`, `/dashboard`, `/reseller` under canonical names; middleware scopes by panel; subscriber portal at tenant hostname (Dashboard/portal layout); Agency/Partner schema-aware, feature-flagged. (§B3, §B12)
- [ ] **Tenant onboarding wizard (T-TNR)** — legal name, branding, support contacts, market/site structure, tax, payment model, provider config, staff, notification prefs, service-plan catalogue, first network site; dependency status (WorkOS membership, DNS, connector, RADIUS client, payment sandbox, messaging, imports, go-live); drafts + validation + change history + approval. (§B5)
- [ ] **CSV onboarding imports** — templates, validation, duplicate detection, dry-run + error export, reviewer approval, idempotent run IDs, reconciliation, audit; subscribers/services/invoices/opening balances/routers/APs/agents/vouchers/historical data; recoverable or reverted as one tracked operation. (§B5)
- [ ] **Customer portal (T-PRT)** — mobile-first; service state + restriction reason + amount due + next action; usage/session history, invoices, receipts, verified payments, plan options, device management, contact updates, vouchers, tickets, announcements, communication prefs; never exposes staff/infra/raw accounting/secrets. (§B9)
- [ ] **Hotspot & captive portal (T-HOT)** — built from the canonical [[../captive-portal-specification|Captive Portal Specification]] in the standalone `captive-portal/` repo folder (core/, ui/, templates/, i18n/, config/, api/, terms/, test/) mounted as `app/(portal)/hotspot/**` route stubs + `convex/portal/` adapters. **MVP auth**: voucher, phone+SMS OTP, MAC/HTTP-cookie, IP binding. **Reconnection**: detection ladder (session/mac-cookie → registered device → phone prompt → manual fallbacks voucher/OTP/QR/credentials) with welcome-back dashboard. **Free trial**: one-time per device/phone with tenant-configurable reset window (`claim → reclaimableAt`). **Payments**: in-portal M-Pesa STK Push with `intent → callback verify → reconcile → entitlement → network job → CoA/reauth → verified connected` and application-vs-network state (`payment_confirmed / provisioning / connected / reconnection_failed`). **Branding**: template + color/logo/background/font/language overrides. **Splash**: terms + privacy + optional operator splash; no third-party ad platform in MVP. **Devices**: self-service list/rename/remove, per-plan limits. **Analytics**: core (visits, attempts, method usage, redemption, conversion, sessions). **MikroTik**: Convex-direct RouterOS API first (approval-gated automation); FreeRADIUS upstream is the Phase 7 upgrade path — this resolves the old Phase 6↔7 circular dependency (portal UI no longer depends on N-AAA being built first). (§B9, §B15)

## Phase 7 — RADIUS, connectors, routers, accounting, CoA, HA (N-AAA, N-ACC, N-COA, N-RAD, N-SES, N-IP, N-WRK, N-CON, N-RT, N-LAB, T-NOC, T-SES)

- [ ] **FreeRADIUS package (N-AAA/N-LAB)** — `services/radius`: config, modules, dictionaries, committed fixtures (Request → Response); auth methods PAP/CHAP/MS-CHAPv2/EAP/EAP-TLS/PEAP/EAP-TTLS/MAC/cert/voucher/captive; PPPoE + Hotspot first. (§B7, §B8)
- [ ] **Local auth path** — authN/authZ from PostgreSQL policy replicas + Redis cache; subscriber access never depends on Convex/Vercel. (§B7, §B8)
- [ ] **RadSec/VPN transport (N-RAD)** — RadSec preferred; UDP only via approved VPN; per-NAS secrets with rotation; NAS client registry with `tenantId` + site scope. (§B7, §B8)
- [ ] **Accounting pipeline (N-ACC)** — Start/Interim/Stop, correlation, dedupe, rollover, missing-Stop, stale-session handling, NAS restarts; partitioned tenant-filtered tables; queues + DLQ. (§B7, §B16)
- [ ] **CoA/Disconnect (N-COA)** — controlled, rate-limited, audited, verified against live NAS/session state. (§B7, §B8)
- [ ] **Go network worker (N-WRK)** — RouterOS API/SNMP/SSH/provisioning/CoA/backups/telemetry; idempotent (job-id upserts), Secrets Manager at start + rotation, least-privilege IAM, dry-run + verified-completion. (§B6, §B18)
- [ ] **Edge connector (N-CON)** — convert existing collector to mTLS connector model: no inbound port, rotation/revocation audit, signed results. (§B6)
- [ ] **Router/NAS/AP onboarding (T-NOC)** — router wizard Monitoring + RADIUS-ready modes; generated templates for review (no unattended push at launch; two-person approval for high risk); AP vendor adapters (MikroTik, Ubiquiti, Cambium, TP-Link, Aruba, Ruckus) with SNMP fallback; discovery review before approval; drift/backup/health. (§B6)
- [ ] **IP pools & IPAM (N-IP)** — IPv4/IPv6 pools, assignments, static IPs, VLAN scoping. (§B7, §B15)
- [ ] **Session management (N-SES)** — active/stale/terminated/failed views, search, per-client disconnect, session history, duplicate/stale detection, per-session record fields per proposal §8. (§B7)
- [ ] **Usage & quotas (T-SES)** — time/data/daily/monthly/per-device/shared quotas, fair-use, rollover, warning/hard/soft limits, threshold-triggered policy change, usage surfaced in portal/invoices/reports/APIs. (§B7; proposal §9)
- [ ] **RADIUS lab + failover acceptance (N-LAB/X-LAB)** — PPPoE + Hotspot, RadSec/VPN, NAS restriction, accounting behaviors, stale sessions, CoA reliability, policy-version accuracy, quota enforcement, connector rotation, worker retry, active-active failover, degraded-mode. (§B19, §B14)

## Phase 8 — Infrastructure, observability, API, operations (X-IAC, X-MON, X-API, X-OPS, X-FRD, T-RPT, T-EXP)

- [ ] **Terraform AWS foundation** — VPC/private subnets/NAT/Fargate/RDS Multi-AZ/Redis/SQS/EventBridge/DLQ/S3/Secrets Manager/KMS/Cloudflare; remote state with locking; reviewed plans. (§B8, §B12)
- [ ] **Resilience targets instrumented** — 99.95% availability, RPO 15 min, RTO 4 h; Cape Town primary with disclosed DR; PITR + backups + restore tests + DR drill recorded. (§B8)
- [ ] **Redis ephemeral plane** — OTP, rate limits, locks, dedupe, short-lived auth cache; tenant-namespaced keys; atomic ops; never system of record. (§B8)
- [ ] **OpenTelemetry end-to-end (X-MON)** — FreeRADIUS, Go worker, PostgreSQL, Redis, Next.js/Convex emit traces/metrics/logs (`service.name`, `tenantId`, `layer`); CloudWatch sink, managed Prom/Grafana, Sentry with tenant context redacted; signal list per Master §B13 incl. auth RPS, accounting RPS, concurrency, response time, rejection/failure rates. (§B13)
- [ ] **Runbooks** — tenant onboarding, WorkOS role/membership, support elevation, payment outage, RADIUS node failure, accounting backlog, connector compromise, cert rotation, router change review, provider webhook failure, data restore, security incident, planned maintenance; each: owner, evidence, escalation, rollback, post-incident review. (§B13)
- [ ] **Key & secret rotation live** — DB passwords, router/API creds, connector certs, collector identities rotate; workers refresh on rotation; scanning green. (§B8, §B13)
- [ ] **Fraud & abuse controls (X-FRD)** — detectors per Master §B12 + proposal §14; concurrent limits, MAC binding, velocity, quarantines, review queues, step-up; explainable alerts only. (§B12)
- [ ] **Public/partner API (X-API)** — versioned REST/OpenAPI (+ optional GraphQL), scoped machine credentials, tenant isolation, pagination/filter/sort, idempotency, rate limits, tracing, structured errors, webhooks + event subscriptions, agreed event names, SDKs. (§B18)
- [ ] **Administration & configuration (X-OPS)** — full config surface with drafts/validation/approval/versioning/rollback/change history/env separation. (§B15, proposal §23)
- [ ] **Reporting (T-RPT) + exports (T-EXP)** — full Master report list; scheduled delivery; role-scoped export. (§B11)

## Phase 9 — Launch audit, load, controlled cutover

- [ ] **Full acceptance suite** — cross-tenant denial, payment duplicate/reversal, RADIUS failover + stale accounting, backup-restore proof, RPO/RTO drill, webhook signature tests, WorkOS sync tests, Playwright role/tenant tests, a11y, security, load. (§B14, §B19)
- [ ] **10,000-session load test** — concurrent RADIUS/accounting/UI mix with headroom; queue capacity + latency budgets recorded. (stack Architecture summary; §B8)
- [ ] **Cutover plan + supervised windows** — reconciliation, WorkOS role/membership verification, connector credential rotation, RADIUS client validation, payment-to-entitlement smoke test, monitoring, incident ownership, rollback limit, written sign-off. (§B2)
- [ ] **Retire global collector shared secret** — only after all connectors have validated mTLS identities. (§B2, §B6)
- [ ] **Final acceptance report** — environments, evidence per gate, limitations, owner sign-off; build success alone is never a release criterion. (§B14)

## Deferred roadmap

- [ ] **Mobile & field ops (D-MOB)** — Expo admin/tech apps; reopen after pilot with measured need. (stack Deferred)
- [ ] **Fiber GIS + IPAM inventory (D-GIS)** — reopen after pilot. (stack Deferred)
- [ ] **AI (D-AI)** — reopen when data quality is stable; explainable and permissioned. (stack Deferred; Master §B12)
- [ ] **TimescaleDB/ClickHouse (D-TSDB)** — reopen on measured write/query evidence. (stack Deferred)
- [ ] **Diameter readiness (D-DIAM)** — reopen after RadSec/AAA acceptance. (proposal §1)

## Continuous rules (every change)

- Each PR: lint, typecheck, unit/integration tests, `tokens:check`, build, tenant-isolation review, and the "only stack-listed technologies" check against [[../technology-stack|technology stack]].
- Move completed checkboxes to [[done]] with the same anchors; keep task lanes mutually exclusive.
- No payment initiation, RADIUS production traffic, direct router configuration, or provider webhooks without their contract and acceptance evidence.

---
type: reference
status: active
date: 2026-09-11
tags: [mylesnet, auth, rbac, workos, nextjs]
---

# MylesNet Auth Implementation Notes

> Canonical scope for authentication, RBAC, session, and cookie work on `mylesnet-dashboard`. This note is a byte-identical mirror of the repo file `docs/auth/README.md` — keep both in sync. Task register: [[../tasks/active|MylesNet Active Tasks — AUTH lane]] / [[../tasks/backlog|MylesNet Backlog — Authentication lane]].

## Direction (fixed)

- **Workforce identity**: WorkOS AuthKit ([[../../technology-stack|technology stack]]).
- **Subscriber identity**: Auth0 phone-OTP-first (future, S-AUTH). Portal authentication never grants staff/network privileges.
- **Convex is the enforcement plane.** The proxy layer only does optimistic routing; every query/mutation/http route re-checks identity, membership, role, and MFA in Convex. See [[../../Secrets and Key Stores|Secrets and Key Stores]] (no secrets in tables), [[../../Cookie Handling|Cookie Handling]], [[../../CSRF Protection|CSRF Protection]], [[../../Audit Log Standards|Audit Log Standards]], [[../../Role-Based UI Visibility Standards|Role-Based UI Visibility Standards]].
- Canonical panel map: `/platform`, `/admin`, `/dashboard`, `/reseller`, `/agency`, `/partner` ([[../design/rbac-panel-hierarchy/99-mylesnet-orientation|MylesNet Orientation]]).

## Next.js 16 note

`middleware.ts` is deprecated in Next.js 16 and renamed to **`proxy.ts`** (root of the app directory, default-export `proxy(request, event)`, Node runtime). The vault RBAC-routing doc `04-nextjs-middleware-routing-with-rbac.md` predates this; implement its intent with `proxy.ts`. Read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/proxy.md` before edits. Proxy must stay optimistically-optimistic: full session/authorization checks belong in the data layer.

## Files

### Convex (enforcement) — implemented

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `convex/schema.ts` | `authTables()` (WorkOS/AuthKit), `users` (+ `mfaEnrolled`, `mfaEnrolledAt`), `auditLog`, etc. |
| `convex/auth.config.ts` | WorkOS customJWT providers; Convex reads `identity.organizationId` + `subject`. |
| `convex/workos.ts` | `ensureOrgMembership` (role + MFA sync), `getWorkosUserByEmail`, `getWorkosMfaEnrollment`. |
| `convex/workosWebhook.ts` | Event processing: user/membership/invitation/session/role. |
| `convex/http.ts` | Route surface: `/workos/webhook` (HMAC-verified via `convex/lib/workosVerify.ts`), `/collector/ingest`. |
| `convex/lib/auth.ts` | Server guards (`requirePlatformAdmin`, `requirePlatformOwner`, permissions), role resolution, `assertMfaCompliance`. |
| `convex/lib/permissions.ts` | Permission catalogue + system role slugs source of truth. |
| `convex/lib/tenant.ts` | Tenant resolution from WorkOS org membership; bootstrap slug `mylesnet`. |
| `convex/lib/mfa.ts` | Pure MFA policy (mandatory-2FA roles, fail-closed compliance) + `mfa.test.ts`. |
| `convex/platformUsers.ts` | `syncWorkosIdentity` internal mutation (persists MFA mirror). |

### Apps/web (server/edge) — implemented

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `apps/web/proxy.ts` | `authkitMiddleware` public-route allowlist, cookie-password gate. **Extend**: set `__mylesnet_tenant` from hostname; security headers. |
| `apps/web/app/(app)/auth/callback/route.ts` | AuthKit callback with PKCE-replay resilience. |
| `apps/web/app/(app)/signin/route.ts` | Redirect to WorkOS hosted auth. |
| `apps/web/app/components/OrgGuard.tsx` | After-login org membership + role sync orchestrator. |
| `apps/web/app/lib/convex.ts` | Typed Convex client + `ConvexProviderWithAuth`. |

### Apps/web lib (server DAL) — pending this pass

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `apps/web/lib/auth/cookies.ts` | `__mylesnet_*` cookie names/options, tenant + csrf readers (Cookie Handling). |
| `apps/web/lib/auth/csrf.ts` | Per-session double-submit token; header check; 403 on mismatch (CSRF Protection). |
| `apps/web/lib/auth/tenant.ts` | Pure hostname → tenant resolution + cookie helpers (+ test). |
| `apps/web/lib/auth/session.ts` | Server session facade: `getSession`, `requireUser`, `requireRole` over AuthKit token claims (`getTokenClaims`). |
| `apps/web/lib/auth/rbac.ts` | Pure optimistic UI role helpers (has-prefix has-permission) consuming claims. |

## Cookies

- Session cookie: AuthKit-managed (`WORKOS_COOKIE_NAME`, default `wos-session`), httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, rotation on privilege change.
- App cookies: `__mylesnet_tenant` (hostname-resolved tenant slug, set in proxy), `__mylesnet_csrf` (double-submit token, server route only). All: httpOnly where server-only, sameSite=Lax, Secure in prod, clear-on-signout.

## MFA position (2026-09-11)

- WorkOS owns enrollment. App mirrors enrollment onto `users.mfaEnrolled` / `mfaEnrolledAt` at reconcile; `convex/lib/mfa.ts` enforces mandatory 2FA for `platform_owner`, `platform_admin`, `ops_manager`, `finance_manager`; `assertMfaCompliance` fails closed in `requirePlatformAdmin`/`requirePlatformOwner` (shadow mode via RBAC env flags). Full in-app setup UI + WorkOS org-level MFA policy config is backlogged (Phase 2).

 <!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->
 
 # This is NOT the Next.js you know
 
 This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.
 
 This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.
 
 <!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->
 
 ## Agent Skills
 
 This project has access to reusable agent skills from multiple sources:
 
 ### Local Skills (`C:\Users\Admin\.agents\skills\`)
 Core opencode skills for code review, automation, subagents, loops, hooks, and more. Load via `/skill-name` when needed.
 
 ### David Ondrej Skills (`vendor/davidondrej-skills/skills/`)
 Additional agent skills for orchestration, research, thinking, ops, and skill authoring. Reference the `SKILL.md` in each subfolder before use:
 - `agent-orchestration/` - subagents, goal loops, handoffs, git worktrees
 - `research-and-web/` - web/YouTube research (DeepAPI powered)
 - `thinking-and-docs/` - structured thinking, documentation
 - `ops-and-setup/` - server/security setup
 - `skill-authoring/` - create/publish new skills
 
 ### Pre-Task Check
 Before starting any coding task, check available skills in `.agents/skills/` and `vendor/davidondrej-skills/skills/`. Use the most relevant skill for the task.
 
 ## Technology Stack (no drift)
 
 - `docs/technology-stack.md` is the fixed, authoritative technology contract for MylesNet (byte-identical mirror of the vault file `products/mylesnet/technology-stack.md`). Read it before any architecture or dependency decision, and check every proposed change against it.
 - Do not add a new runtime package, service, provider, or infrastructure technology that is not listed there. A justified addition requires (1) a dated decision-log entry, (2) an update to **both** `docs/technology-stack.md` and the vault file, and (3) noting the change in the daily record. Until then it is drift, not an accepted change.
 - Build work converges to the stack's monorepo shape (`apps/`, `convex/`, `services/`, `packages/`, `infrastructure/`) per the migration gates in `docs/architecture/MylesNet_Multi_Tenant_ISP_Radius_SaaS_Technical_Specification_v3.md`. The current single Next.js app is the pre-migration state, not the target.
 - Keep `docs/technology-stack.md` and `docs/architecture/MylesNet_Multi_Tenant_ISP_Radius_SaaS_Technical_Specification_v3.md` identical to their vault sources; a divergence is drift.
 
 ## Captive portal (T-HOT)
 
 - Canonical scope: `docs/captive-portal/captive-portal-specification.md` (byte-identical mirror of the vault `products/mylesnet/captive-portal-specification.md`); flows: `docs/captive-portal/captive-portal-flows.md`. Read these before any captive-portal/hotspot code.
 - Built as a route surface in this app: screens/logic in the `captive-portal/` feature-slice folder, thin stubs in `app/(portal)/hotspot/**`, thin Convex adapters in `convex/portal/`, `@portal/*` alias, tenant resolved by hostname. Do not create a separate portal app.
 - Schema additions (§18) stay centralized in `convex/schema.ts`; no new runtime dependency may be introduced without the Technology Stack (no drift) rule above. Build work has not started (spec approved 2026-09-10; implementation deferred by owner directive).
+
+## Agent threads / transcripts
+
+- `docs/agent-threads/` is the archival home for **notable** agent sessions — a byte-identical mirror of the vault `products/mylesnet/agent-threads/`. Check its `README.md` index at session start for recent context.
+- One thread = one pair: `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` (verbatim transcript with a summary/decision block up top) + `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.json` (structured twin for querying).
+- Archive only notable sessions (decisions, approvals, audits, investigations). Whenever one materially changes the product, record it here **and** copy both files identical into the vault `products/mylesnet/agent-threads/` (vault canonical); a divergence is drift.

# Cookie Handling

[[Cookie Handling]] is mandatory for every [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] product and client project. It applies to [[WorkOS AuthKit]] sessions, tenant context, [[CSRF Protection]], onboarding state, temporary state, and any future server-set cookie.

## Cookie Security Standards

Every cookie set by a system must include all of these attributes:

- `httpOnly: true`
- `secure: true`
- `sameSite: "lax"` by default
- `path: "/"`
- `domain` explicitly set to the correct product or panel domain
- `maxAge` or `expires`

Use `sameSite: "strict"` for sensitive operations where cross-site redirects are not required.

## Never Do

- Never set a cookie without `httpOnly` unless client-side JavaScript access is explicitly required and documented in a code comment.
- Never set a cookie without `maxAge` or `expires`.
- Never store sensitive data in a cookie value. Store only a reference ID.
- Never store plaintext tokens, roles, permissions, tenant data, user data, or provider secrets in cookies.
- Never set auth cookies from client-side JavaScript.
- Never use `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` for auth tokens.
- Never set `secure: false`, including in development.
- Never use generic cookie names such as `session`, `token`, `auth`, or `user`.

## Naming Convention

Cookie names must use this format:

```text
__[product]_[purpose]
```

Examples:

- `__edumyles_session`
- `__edumyles_tenant`
- `__mylescrm_session`
- `__eduryde_session`

## Product Cookie Prefixes

| Product | Cookie prefix | Tenant domain scope | Admin panel scope | Network panel scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [[EduMyles]] | `__edumyles_` | `.edumyles.com` | `admin.edumyles.com` | `network.edumyles.com` |
| [[MylesCRM]] | `__mylescrm_` | `.mylescrm.com` | `admin.mylescrm.com` | `network.mylescrm.com` |
| [[AgriMyles]] | `__agrimyles_` | `.agrimyles.com` | `admin.agrimyles.com` | `network.agrimyles.com` |
| [[MylesCare]] | `__mylescare_` | `.mylescare.com` | `admin.mylescare.com` | `network.mylescare.com` |
| [[MylesProp]] | `__mylesprop_` | `.mylesprop.com` | `admin.mylesprop.com` | `network.mylesprop.com` |
| [[EduRyde]] | `__eduryde_` | `.eduryde.com` | `admin.eduryde.com` | `network.eduryde.com` |
| [[MylesNet]] | `__mylesnet_` | `.mylesnet.com` | `admin.mylesnet.com` | `network.mylesnet.com` |
| [[PhysioHome]] | `__physiohome_` | Not confirmed | Not confirmed | Not confirmed |
| School website clients | `__school_[slug]_` | Client domain | `admin.[domain]` (Premium) | N/A |

School website cookie rules: [[CRM/leads/School Website Technical Specification#Cookie and Consent Policy (School Sites)|School Website Technical Specification]]. Footer: [[School Website Footer Standards]].

If a final production domain differs from this table, update the relevant product decision note and this table before implementation.

## Lifetime Rules

| Cookie type | MaxAge | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Auth session through [[WorkOS AuthKit]] | 24 hours | Refreshed on activity |
| Remember me session | 30 days | Only with explicit user opt-in |
| Tenant context | Same as session | Cleared with session |
| Onboarding state | 7 days | Non-sensitive and cleared after completion |
| CSRF token | Per request | Single use and cleared immediately after use |
| Temporary state | 15 minutes | Form state or wizard progress |

## Automatic Cookie Clearing

The system must clear cookies server-side in middleware and relevant [[Next.js]] route handlers.

Required clearing events:

- Sign out: delete all `__[product]_*` cookies immediately on the server, then redirect to `/login`.
- Session expiry: clear cookies before redirecting to `/login`.
- [[WorkOS AuthKit]] role change or membership revocation: clear session cookies and force re-authentication.
- Tenant switch: clear tenant context before setting the new context.
- Password change or account deactivation: invalidate active [[WorkOS]] sessions and clear cookies across all panels.
- Master Admin and Super Admin browser close: use session cookies only with no persistence.
- Admin inactivity timeout: clear after 30 minutes of inactivity.
- Tenant app inactivity timeout: clear after 2 hours of inactivity.
- Suspicious activity: clear partial auth cookies, clear mismatched tenant cookies, clear tampered cookies, force re-authentication, and log the incident server-side.

Show a warning modal 5 minutes before inactivity expiry. On timeout, redirect to `/login` with: `Your session expired due to inactivity. Please sign in again.`

## Server-Side Clearing Pattern

Use this pattern in [[Next.js]] middleware or route handlers:

```ts
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";

const clearAuthCookies = (response: NextResponse, product: string) => {
  const cookiesToClear = [
    `__${product}_session`,
    `__${product}_tenant`,
  ];

  cookiesToClear.forEach((name) => {
    response.cookies.set(name, "", {
      httpOnly: true,
      secure: true,
      sameSite: "lax",
      path: "/",
      maxAge: 0,
      expires: new Date(0),
    });
  });

  return response;
};
```

Never use `response.cookies.delete()` alone. Always set an empty value with `maxAge: 0` and `expires: new Date(0)`.

## Cross-Subdomain Handling

For tenant subdomains such as `[tenant].[product].com`:

- Set tenant app session cookie domain to `.[product].com` when it must be shared across tenant subdomains.
- Keep tenant context specific to the current subdomain.
- Master Admin cookies must be scoped only to `admin.[product].com`.
- Super Admin cookies must be scoped only to `network.[product].com`.
- Admin and network cookies must not be valid on tenant subdomains.

## CSRF Protection

Every `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` route must use [[CSRF Protection]]:

- Generate one CSRF token per session and store it in an HttpOnly cookie.
- Require the token as a request header on every state-changing request.
- Validate the token server-side before any mutation.
- Rotate the token after every use.
- Never accept a state-changing request without a valid token.

## Cookie Audit

At the end of every session where cookies are touched, verify:

- [ ] All cookies have `httpOnly: true`.
- [ ] All cookies have `secure: true`.
- [ ] All cookies have `sameSite` set explicitly.
- [ ] All cookies have `maxAge` or `expires` set.
- [ ] Sign-out clears all cookies server-side.
- [ ] Session expiry clears all cookies server-side.
- [ ] No sensitive data is stored in cookie values.
- [ ] No generic cookie names are used.
- [ ] All cookie names are prefixed with `__[product]_`.
- [ ] Cross-subdomain scope matches product architecture.
- [ ] [[CSRF Protection]] is implemented on all mutating routes.

## Related Notes

- [[Security]]
- [[CSRF Protection]]
- [[WorkOS AuthKit]]
- [[Next.js]]
- [[Secrets And Environment Variables]]

# CSRF Protection

[[CSRF Protection]] is required for every state-changing request in [[MylesCorp Technologies Ltd]] products and client projects.

## Required Routes

Every `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` route in all three panels (Master Admin `admin.[product].com`, Super Admin `network.[product].com`, and Tenant App `[tenant].[product].com`) must validate a CSRF token server-side before executing a mutation.

## Required Behavior

- Generate a token per session.
- Store the token in an HttpOnly secure cookie.
- Require the token in a request header.
- Rotate the token after every successful use.
- Reject missing, expired, reused, or invalid tokens.
- Clear invalid or tampered CSRF cookies server-side.

1: ---
2: title: cookies
3: description: API Reference for the cookies function.
4: ---
5: 
6: `cookies` is an **async** function that allows you to read the HTTP incoming request cookies in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), and read/write outgoing request cookies in [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
7: 
8: ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
9: import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
10: 
11: export default async function Page() {
12:   const cookieStore = await cookies()
13:   const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
14:   return '...'
15: }
16: ```
17: 
18: ```js filename="app/page.js" switcher
19: import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
20: 
21: export default async function Page() {
22:   const cookieStore = await cookies()
23:   const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
24:   return '...'
25: }
26: ```
27: 
28: ## Reference
29: 
30: ### Methods
31: 
32: The following methods are available:
33: 
34: | Method                      | Return Type      | Description                                                                     |
35: | --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
36: | `get('name')`               | Object           | Accepts a cookie name and returns an object with the name and value.            |
37: | `getAll()`                  | Array of objects | Returns a list of all the cookies with a matching name.                         |
38: | `has('name')`               | Boolean          | Accepts a cookie name and returns a boolean based on if the cookie exists.      |
39: | `set(name, value, options)` | -                | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. |
40: | `delete(name)`              | -                | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie.                                   |
41: | `toString()`                | String           | Returns a string representation of the cookies.                                 |
42: 
43: ### Options
44: 
45: When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported:
46: 
47: | Option        | Type                                   | Description                                                                        |
48: | ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
49: | `name`        | String                                 | Specifies the name of the cookie.                                                  |
50: | `value`       | String                                 | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie.                                    |
51: | `expires`     | Date                                   | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire.                                |
52: | `maxAge`      | Number                                 | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds.                                             |
53: | `domain`      | String                                 | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available.                                |
54: | `path`        | String, default: `'/'`                 | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain.                    |
55: | `secure`      | Boolean                                | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security.         |
56: | `httpOnly`    | Boolean                                | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access.              |
57: | `sameSite`    | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior.                                 |
58: | `priority`    | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority                                                    |
59: | `partitioned` | Boolean                                | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). |
60: 
61: The only option with a default value is `path`.
62: 
63: To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies).
64: 
65: ## Good to know
66: 
67: - `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies.
68:   - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.
69: - `cookies` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in a layout or page will opt a route into [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering).
70: - With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), calling `cookies()` outside of a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary prevents the route from being prerendered. See [Next.js encountered runtime data during prerendering](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-runtime) for fix options.
71: - The `.delete` method can only be called:
72:   - In a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
73:   - If it belongs to the same domain from which `.set` is called. For wildcard domains, the specific subdomain must be an exact match. Additionally, the code must be executed on the same protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) as the cookie you want to delete.
74: - HTTP does not allow setting cookies after streaming starts, so you must use `.set` in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
75: 
76: ## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Components
77: 
78: When working with cookies in Server Components, it's important to understand that cookies are fundamentally a client-side storage mechanism:
79: 
80: - **Reading cookies** works in Server Components because you're accessing the cookie data that the client's browser sends to the server in the HTTP request headers.

export default async function Page() {
  const cookieStore = await cookies()

  return '...'

```

## Reference

### Methods

The following methods are available:

| Method                      | Return Type      | Description                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get('name')`               | Object           | Accepts a cookie name and returns an object with the name and value.            |
| `getAll()`                  | Array of objects | Returns a list of all the cookies with a matching name.                         |
| `has('name')`               | Boolean          | Accepts a cookie name and returns a boolean based on if the cookie exists.      |
| `set(name, value, options)` | -                | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. |
| `delete(name)`              | -                | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie.                                   |
| `toString()`                | String           | Returns a string representation of the cookies.                                 |

### Options

When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported:

| Option        | Type                                   | Description                                                                        |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | String                                 | Specifies the name of the cookie.                                                  |
| `value`       | String                                 | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie.                                    |
| `expires`     | Date                                   | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire.                                |
| `maxAge`      | Number                                 | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds.                                             |
| `domain`      | String                                 | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available.                                |
| `path`        | String, default: `'/'`                 | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain.                    |
| `secure`      | Boolean                                | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security.         |
| `httpOnly`    | Boolean                                | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access.              |
| `sameSite`    | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior.                                 |
| `priority`    | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority                                                    |
| `partitioned` | Boolean                                | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). |

The only option with a default value is `path`.

To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies).

## Good to know

- `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies.
  - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.
- `cookies` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in a layout or page will opt a route into [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering).
- With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), calling `cookies()` outside of a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary prevents the route from being prerendered. See [Next.js encountered runtime data during prerendering](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-runtime) for fix options.
- The `.delete` method can only be called:
  - In a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
  - If it belongs to the same domain from which `.set` is called. For wildcard domains, the specific subdomain must be an exact match. Additionally, the code must be executed on the same protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) as the cookie you want to delete.
- HTTP does not allow setting cookies after streaming starts, so you must use `.set` in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Components

When working with cookies in Server Components, it's important to understand that cookies are fundamentally a client-side storage mechanism:

- **Reading cookies** works in Server Components because you're accessing the cookie data that the client's browser sends to the server in the HTTP request headers.

First, the pure ones (testable): csrf.ts core, tenant.ts core, rbac.ts — all export pure functions. cookies.ts provides constants + option builders (pure) plus server wrapper functions (async, using next/headers). session.ts is the server facade.

Let me create:

**apps/web/lib/auth/cookies.ts**
- Constants: TENANT_COOKIE_NAME = "__mylesnet_tenant", CSRF_COOKIE_NAME = "__mylesnet_csrf".
- cookieOptions(overrides): pure builder returning { httpOnly, secure, sameSite, path, maxAge } with required attributes. domain left to caller (may be undefined in dev/localhost, fine to omit — spec says explicitly set to correct domain; caller passes domain). Provide `getCookieDomain(host)` similar? The vault requires `domain` explicitly set. I'll accept a `domain` override parameter defaulting from env `MYLESNET_COOKIE_DOMAIN`. Add that to .env.example.
- Server functions (async): getTenantCookie(), setTenantCookie(slug, options), clearAuthCookies() (set empty maxAge 0 + expires epoch — per "Never use delete() alone"), getCsrfCookie(), setCsrfCookie(token).

**apps/web/lib/auth/csrf.ts**
- Pure: verifyCsrfToken(cookieValue, headerValue): boolean (constant-time), TOKEN_LENGTH, RE_CSRF_TOKEN regex.
- generateCsrfToken(): uses node crypto `randomBytes` — this is fine in Node runtime; in edge (proxy) it'd be `crypto.getRandomValues`. Keep a Node import from "node:crypto"? Actually Next server code can use global crypto (WebCrypto) in both node and edge. Use `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32))` → base64url. That works everywhere.
- Server: requireValidCsrf(request): for route handlers reading headers + cookie (both async) → returns token cookie to set (rotation) or throws 403.
- Server: getOrCreateCsrfToken() for server functions that need to send token to client via header? For double-submit, the client reads the cookie (httpOnly can't be read by JS!). Standard says CSRF token cookie should be HttpOnly? Cookie Handling standard: "Generate one CSRF token per session and store it in an HttpOnly cookie." But double-submit needs the JS app to read the token to echo back in a header. If the cookie is httpOnly, JS can't read it. The CSRF Protection standard says store in HttpOnly cookie. Hmm. The vault standards conflict with the classic double-submit approach. Options: store CSRF token in non-httpOnly cookie for JS to read (standard double-submit), but the Cookie Handling standard explicitly demands httpOnly and "Never set a cookie without httpOnly unless client-side JavaScript access is explicitly required and documented in a code comment." So there's allowance: JS access explicitly required → document in comment. So CSRF cookie is the documented exception: name `__mylesnet_csrf`, httpOnly false (JS must read for double-submit), documented comment. That satisfies both standards (the "Never" clause has the explicit exception clause).

Given the existing app likely uses Convex mutations (server actions / convex through AJAX) — how do they get the CSRF token? The Convex client functions run from browser to the Convex cloud; the app's own route handlers/actions are where CSRF matters. For the near-term, I'll implement the cookie + header verification utilities and a helper to read the token from cookie (non-httpOnly so JS can include it). I'll document the exception.

parts.text:
The Security Standards don't specify the exact security header set. I'll apply a sensible, non-breaking standard set and document it. Keep it minimal and safe:

- Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains (only set when request is https, to avoid localhost issues — actually setting on http responses can break; set unconditionally is common but better gate on secure. I'll set it unconditionally with comments; Vercel prod is https. If insecure localhost receives it, browsers ignore HSTS for http anyway.) 
- X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
- Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
- X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN (frame-ancestors not available as header in all browsers; X-Frame-Options is legacy but fine and doesn't break our own app)
- Permissions-Policy: allowlists minimal? Setting a restrictive Permissions-Policy can break features. Keep it: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(self), payment=(self). Modest.
- Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin? Could break OAuth popups? WorkOS AuthKit uses full-page redirects, not popups, so COOP same-origin is safe, but to be conservative I'll skip COOP/COEP/CORP to avoid breaking CDN assets.

Skip CSP (can break Next app with inline scripts/styles + CDN fonts) — note it as future work.

Now write proxy.ts extension. Set tenant cookie only when slug resolved AND response is not a redirect? Setting cookies on redirect responses works fine. But careful: for unauthenticated paths (marketing pages), not logged in — still fine to set tenant cookie. But if authkit returned a redirect to signin for protected route, we still attach tenant cookie — harmless.

One safety: only set if slug differs from existing request cookie to avoid overriding? Minor. Keep simple: set if slug exists.

Also note the NextRequest host: In proxy, request.nextUrl.hostname gives the host. Use that. But behind Vercel, `x-forwarded-host` may carry the host. request.nextUrl.hostname reflects the Host header. Good enough.

One concern: `toBase64Url` uses `btoa` — available in Node 24 globally? Node has global `btoa` since v16. Yes. In Next server runtime (Node), global btoa exists. In Edge runtime — also exists. OK.

Another concern: csrf.test.ts asserts `toBase64Url(new Uint8Array([0xff, 0x00, 0x3d, 0xfb]))` equals "___9-". Let me verify: bytes 255,0,61,251 -> binary 11111111 00000000 00111101 11111011. Base64 encoding of 4 bytes = ceil(4/3)=2 groups → 8 chars total (2 sextet triplets = 6 chars from 3 bytes + 2 chars from last byte + pad). Actually 4 bytes -> first 3 bytes (255,0,61): 111111 110000 000000 111101 = "/wA9". Last byte 251 = 11111011 -> 111110 11(0000) = "-w==". So full " /wA9-w==" → base64url " /wA9-w" → replace +/= → "/wA9-w". Hmm that's not "___9-". Let me recompute: 255=11111111, 0=00000000, 61=00111101, 251=11111011.

Concatenated bits: 11111111 00000000 00111101 11111011
Split into 6-bit groups: 111111,110000,000000,111101,111110,110000(pad with zeros to make last group: last byte 11111011 → we have 32 bits, 32/6=5.33 → 6 groups → 36 bits, pad 4 zeros).
bits: 11111111 00000000 00111101 11111011 0000
groups: 
111111=63 "=" -> base64 "=" index63 -> "/"
110000=48 -> "w"
000000=0 -> "A"
111101=61 -> "9"
111110=62 -> "+"
110000=48 -> "w"
So encoded = "/wA9+w==" → url-safe "%2FwA9%2Bw==" → replace: "/"->"_", "+"->"-" → "_wA9-w==", strip "=" → "_wA9-w".

So my test assertion "___9-" is WRONG. Actual is "_wA9-w". Let me fix the test.
